title.zh: 卷一百七十 列傳第五十七: 尚文 申屠致遠 雷膺 胡祗遹 王利用 暢師文 張炤 袁裕 張昉 郝彬 高源 楊湜 吳鼎 梁德珪
title.en: Volume 170 Biographies 57: Shang Wen, Shen Tuzhiyuan, Lei Ying, Hu Zhi Yu, Wang Liyong, Chang Shiwen, Zhang Zhao, Yuan Yu, Zhang Fang, Hao Bin, Gao Yuan, Yang Shi, Wu Ding, Liang Degui
title.raw: 卷一百七十 列傳第五十七: 尚文 申屠致遠 雷膺 胡祗遹 王利用 暢師文 張炤 袁裕 張昉 郝彬 高源 楊湜 吳鼎 梁德珪 Volume 170 Biographies 57: Shang Wen, Shen Tuzhiyuan, Lei Ying, Hu ZhiYu, Wang Liyong, Chang Shiwen, Zhang Zhao, Yuan Yu, Zhang Fang, Hao Bin, Gao Yuan, Yang Shi, Wu Ding, Liang Degui

sentences.zh: 尚文，字周卿，世為祁州深澤人，後徙保定，遂佔籍焉。

translations.literal: Shang Wen, styled Zhouqing, for generations was a man of Shenze in Qizhou; later he moved to Baoding and there registered as a local resident.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Wen, whose courtesy name was Zhouqing, came from a family long established at Shenze in Qizhou; they later moved to Baoding and took up household registration there.

sentences.zh: 文幼穎悟，負奇志。

translations.literal: Wen in youth was keenly intelligent and bore an uncommon ambition.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy, Wen was unusually quick-witted and nursed uncommon ambitions.

sentences.zh: 張文謙宣撫河東，參政王椅薦其才，遂辟掌書記。

translations.literal: When Zhang Wenqian was pacification commissioner of Hedong, Vice Administrator Wang Yi recommended his talent, and he was recruited as secretary in charge of records.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhang Wenqian served as pacification commissioner of Hedong, Vice Administrator Wang Yi recommended his abilities, and Wen was recruited as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 未幾，西夏行中書省復辟之。

translations.literal: Before long the Western Xia Branch Secretariat again recruited him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Branch Secretariat for Western Xia recruited him again.

sentences.zh: 至元六年，始立朝儀，太保劉秉忠言於世祖，詔文與諸儒，採唐《開元禮》及近代禮儀之可行於今者，斟酌損益，凡文武儀仗、服色差等，皆文掌焉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan court ritual was first established; Grand Guardian Liu Bingzhong spoke to the Founder, who ordered Wen together with various scholars to take from the Tang Kaiyuan Ritual and recent rituals practicable today, weigh additions and reductions, and Wen had charge of all civil and military insignia, dress grades, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Zhiyuan reign, court ceremony was established for the first time. Grand Guardian Liu Bingzhong advised Kublai, who ordered Wen and other scholars to draw on the Tang Kaiyuan Ritual and on recent rites still applicable, adjusting them as needed; Wen oversaw all civil and military regalia, ranks of dress, and related matters.

sentences.zh: 七年春二月，朝儀成，百官肄習，帝臨觀之，大悅，遂為定制。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring in the seventh year the court ritual was completed; the hundred officials practiced it, the emperor came in person to observe, was greatly pleased, and it was made the fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring in the seventh year the court ceremonies were complete. Officials rehearsed them while the emperor watched in person, was greatly pleased, and made them the permanent standard.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，立侍儀司，擢右直侍儀使，轉司農都事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter the Directorate of Ceremonial Attendants was established; he was promoted to Right Direct Attendant of Ceremonies and transferred to be chief clerk of the Directorate of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter the Directorate of Ceremonial Attendants was established; he was promoted to Right Direct Attendant of Ceremonies, then transferred to chief clerk in the Directorate of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 十七年，出守輝州。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he went out to govern Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was sent out to serve as prefect of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 時河朔大旱，輝獨以禱得雨，境內大稔。

translations.literal: At the time there was great drought north of the Yellow River; Huizhou alone obtained rain through prayer, and within the jurisdiction there was a great harvest.
translations.idiomatic: A severe drought gripped the region north of the Yellow River, but Huizhou alone received rain after Wen prayed for it, and the prefecture enjoyed a bumper harvest.

sentences.zh: 懷孟民馬氏、宋氏，誣伏殺人，積歲獄不能決，提刑使者命文讞以論報。

translations.literal: The Ma and Song clans of Huaimeng, under false confession of murder, had cases unresolved for years; the judicial investigation commissioner ordered Wen to judge and report sentence.
translations.idiomatic: The Ma and Song families of Huaimeng had falsely confessed to murder, and their cases had dragged on for years without resolution. The judicial investigation commissioner ordered Wen to review the files and pronounce sentence.

sentences.zh: 文推跡究情，得獄吏、獄卒羅織狀，兩獄皆釋。

translations.literal: Wen traced and investigated the facts, obtained evidence that jail clerks and jailers had framed them, and both cases were released.
translations.idiomatic: Wen traced the facts to their root and found that jail clerks and guards had fabricated the charges; both prisoners were released.

sentences.zh: 十九年，進戶部郎中，奏罷懷、衛竹稅提舉司，民便之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and memorialized to abolish the Huai and Wei Bamboo Tax Intendant Office; the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and memorialized to abolish the bamboo-tax intendant offices for Huai and Wei; the people benefited.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，除御史臺都事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed chief clerk of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was appointed chief clerk of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 行台御史上封事，言上春秋高，宜禪位皇太子。

translations.literal: A Branch Secretariat censor submitted a sealed memorial saying the emperor's years were advanced and he ought to abdicate in favor of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: A censor of the Branch Secretariat submitted a sealed memorial arguing that the emperor was advanced in years and ought to abdicate in favor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子聞之懼，中台秘其章不發。

translations.literal: The crown prince, hearing of it, was afraid; the Central Secretariat kept the memorial secret and did not issue it.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was alarmed when he heard of it, and the Central Secretariat kept the memorial secret without forwarding it.

sentences.zh: 答即古阿散等知之，請收內外百司吏案，大索天下埋沒錢糧，而實欲發其事，乃悉拘封御史臺吏案。

translations.literal: Dajigahasun and others learned of it, requested to seize the clerk files of all offices within and without, and greatly search the realm for concealed grain and funds, but in truth wished to expose the matter, and therefore detained and sealed all Censorate clerk files.
translations.idiomatic: Dajigahasun and his faction learned of the memorial and petitioned to seize the personnel files of every office, ostensibly to hunt nationwide for concealed revenues, but in truth to expose the abdication proposal; they had all Censorate files impounded and sealed.

sentences.zh: 文拘留秘章不與，答即古聞於帝，命宗正薛徹幹取其章。

translations.literal: Wen detained the secret memorial and would not hand it over; Dajigahasun reported to the emperor, who ordered Director of the Imperial Clan Xue Chegan to take the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Wen held back the secret memorial and refused to surrender it. Dajigahasun reported this to the emperor, who ordered Director of the Imperial Clan Xue Chegan to seize it.

sentences.zh: 文曰：「事急矣！」

translations.literal: Wen said: "The matter is urgent!"
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, "The situation is urgent!"

sentences.zh: 即白御史大夫曰：「是欲上危太子，下陷大臣，流毒天下之民，其謀至姦也。

translations.literal: He immediately reported to the Censor-in-Chief: "This is intended to endanger the crown prince above, trap ministers below, and spread poison among the people of the realm; the plot is utterly treacherous.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately told the Censor-in-Chief, "Their aim is to endanger the crown prince from above, entrap the ministers below, and bring harm to the people throughout the realm. The scheme is utterly treacherous.

sentences.zh: 且答即古乃阿合馬餘黨，贓罪狼籍，宜先發以奪其謀。」

translations.literal: Moreover Dajigahasun is a remnant partisan of Ahmad, his corrupt crimes are notorious; he should be exposed first to frustrate his plot."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Dajigahasun is a holdover from Ahmad's faction, his record of corruption is notorious, and we should strike first to break their plot."

sentences.zh: 大夫遂與丞相相議，即入言狀，帝震怒曰：「汝等無罪耶？」

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief then consulted with the chief councillor, immediately entered and reported the situation; the emperor was greatly angered and said: "Are you yourselves without guilt?"
translations.idiomatic: The Censor-in-Chief conferred with the chief councillor and at once reported the matter to the throne. The emperor flew into a rage and said, "Are you yourselves without guilt?"

sentences.zh: 丞相進曰：「臣等無所逃罪，但此輩名載刑書，此舉動搖人心，宜選重臣為之長，庶靖紛擾。」

translations.literal: The chief councillor advanced and said: "We ministers have no escape from guilt, but these men's names are recorded in the penal code; this action shakes people's hearts; a weighty minister ought to be chosen as their head, so that disturbance may be calmed."
translations.idiomatic: The chief councillor stepped forward and said, "We cannot escape blame, but these men are already named in the penal statutes. Their maneuver is unsettling the court. Appoint a senior minister to head the investigation, and the turmoil may be quieted."

sentences.zh: 帝怒稍解，可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger eased somewhat and he approved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger eased somewhat, and he approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 既而答即古受人金，與其黨竟坐姦贓論死，其機實自文發之。

translations.literal: Before long Dajigahasun was found to have taken bribes; he and his faction were finally sentenced to death for treachery and corruption; the opening move in truth came from Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Dajigahasun was found to have taken bribes, and he and his associates were condemned to death for treachery and corruption. The initiative had in fact come from Wen.

sentences.zh: 升大司農丞，轉少卿，遷吏部侍郎，改江南湖北道肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture, transferred to Junior Director, moved to Vice Minister of Personnel, and changed to Surveillance Commissioner of the Jiangnan-Hubei Circuit for Purging Corruption.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture, then Junior Director, then Vice Minister of Personnel, and was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of the Jiangnan-Hubei Circuit for Purging Corruption.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，召為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was summoned as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was summoned to serve as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 元貞初，拜中台侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanzhen he was appointed Attending Censor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yuanzhen reign he was appointed Attending Censor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時行台御史及浙西憲司劾江浙行省平章不法者十七事，制遣文往詰之。

translations.literal: At the time Branch Secretariat censors and the Zhexi Surveillance Commission impeached the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat's Grand Administrator for seventeen unlawful acts; by decree Wen was sent to interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: Censors of the Branch Secretariat and the Zhexi Surveillance Commission had impeached the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat's Grand Administrator on seventeen counts of misconduct. An imperial order sent Wen to investigate.

sentences.zh: 左驗明著，猶力爭不服，文以上聞，平章乃言御史違制取會防鎮軍數。

translations.literal: Though the evidence on the left was clear, he still strove and would not submit; Wen reported upward, and the Grand Administrator then said the censors had violated regulations in obtaining tallies of garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Even with the evidence plainly against him, the Grand Administrator still fought the charges. Wen reported to the throne, whereupon the Grand Administrator countered that the censors had violated regulations by obtaining tallies of garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 成宗命省台大臣雜議，咸曰：「平章勳臣之後，所犯者輕，事宜宥；

translations.literal: Chengzong ordered provincial and censorial grandees to deliberate together; all said: "The Grand Administrator is descendant of a meritorious minister; his offenses are light and ought to be pardoned;
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong ordered senior officials of the secretariat and censorate to deliberate jointly. All agreed: "The Grand Administrator is descended from a meritorious house; his offenses are minor and should be pardoned;

sentences.zh: 御史取會軍數，法當死。」

translations.literal: the censors, in obtaining military tallies, by law ought to die."
translations.idiomatic: the censors, for obtaining military tallies, deserve death by law."

sentences.zh: 文抗言：「平章罪狀明白，不受簿責，無人臣禮，其罪非輕。

translations.literal: Wen protested: "The Grand Administrator's crimes are clear; he would not accept accounting and blame—this lacks the propriety of a minister; his crime is not light.
translations.idiomatic: Wen objected forcefully: "The Grand Administrator's guilt is clear. He refused to accept investigation and showed no deference owed a subject—the offense is not minor.

sentences.zh: 御史糾事之官，因兵卒爭訴，責其帥如籍均役，情無害法，即有罪亦輕。」

translations.literal: Censors are officers who investigate matters; because soldiers disputed and appealed, they demanded their commander follow the register in equalizing corvée—the circumstances do not harm the law, and even if guilty the crime is light."
translations.idiomatic: Censors exist to investigate wrongdoing. They demanded that a commander apportion corvée according to the register because soldiers had petitioned in dispute. The circumstances do no real violence to the law, and even if there is guilt, it is slight."

sentences.zh: 廷辯數四，與省台入奏，帝意始悟，平章、御史各杖遣之。

translations.literal: In court they debated four times; with the secretariat and censorate they entered to report; the emperor's mind was finally enlightened; the Grand Administrator and the censors were each beaten with the staff and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After four rounds of debate in court, Wen and the secretariat and censorate officials reported to the throne. The emperor at last understood the matter, and both the Grand Administrator and the censors were flogged and sent away.

sentences.zh: 其守正不阿類如此。

translations.literal: His upholding what is right and not bending were of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity and refusal to yield were characteristic in this way.

sentences.zh: 元貞二年，建言：「治平之世，不宜數赦；

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanzhen he memorialized: "In an age of good government, amnesties ought not to be frequent;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanzhen he memorialized: "In a time of good order, amnesties should not be issued frequently;

sentences.zh: 不急之役，宜且停罷。」

translations.literal: labors not urgent ought for the present to be halted."
translations.idiomatic: non-urgent labor projects should be suspended for now."

sentences.zh: 咸為成宗所嘉納，授河北河南肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: All were praised and accepted by Chengzong, and he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of the Hebei-Henan Circuit for Purging Corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong praised and adopted all of these proposals and appointed him Surveillance Commissioner of the Hebei-Henan Circuit for Purging Corruption.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，河決蒲口，台檄令文按視防河之策。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade the Yellow River burst at Pukou; the Censorate ordered Wen by dispatch to inspect policies for controlling the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dade the Yellow River broke through at Pukou. The Censorate dispatched Wen to review flood-control policy.

sentences.zh: 文建言：

translations.literal: Wen memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Wen submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 長河萬里西來，其勢湍猛，至盟津而下，地平土疏，移徙不常，失禹故道，為中國患，不知幾千百年矣。

translations.literal: The long river comes ten thousand li from the west; its current is swift and fierce; from Mengjin downward the land is level and the soil loose, shifting without constancy, having lost Yu's ancient course—it has been a calamity to China for who knows how many thousands of years.
translations.idiomatic: The great river flows ten thousand li from the west with a swift, violent current. Below Mengjin the terrain is flat and the soil loose, and the channel shifts constantly, having long since abandoned Yu's ancient course. It has plagued China for untold centuries.

sentences.zh: 自古治河，處得其當，則用力少而患遲；

translations.literal: Since antiquity in controlling the river, when the handling is right, little effort is used and the calamity is slow;
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, when river control has been rightly handled, little labor has been needed and disaster has come slowly;

sentences.zh: 事失其宜，則用力多而患速。

translations.literal: when the matter misses what is fitting, much effort is used and the calamity is swift.
translations.idiomatic: when policy misses the mark, great labor is expended and disaster comes quickly.

sentences.zh: 此不易之定論也。

translations.literal: This is the settled judgment that does not change.
translations.idiomatic: This is an established truth that does not change.

sentences.zh: 今陳留抵睢，東西百有餘里，南岸舊河口十一，已塞者二，自涸者六，通川者三，岸高於水，計六七尺，或四五尺；

translations.literal: Now from Chenliu to Sui, east and west more than a hundred li, on the south bank are eleven old river mouths: two already blocked, six dried of themselves, three open channels; the banks are higher than the water by some six or seven chi, or four or five chi;
translations.idiomatic: From Chenliu to Sui, more than a hundred li east to west, the south bank has eleven old mouths: two already sealed, six that dried up on their own, and three still open. The banks stand six or seven feet above the water in places, or four or five;

sentences.zh: 北岸故堤，其水比田高三四尺，或高下等，大概南高於北，約八九尺，堤安得不壞，水安得不北也！

translations.literal: on the north bank the old dike—the water is three or four chi higher than the fields, or level high and low; broadly the south is higher than the north by about eight or nine chi—how can the dike not break, how can the water not go north!
translations.idiomatic: on the north bank the old levee holds water three or four feet above the fields, or level with them. Overall the south bank stands some eight or nine feet higher than the north. How can the levee hold, and how can the water fail to break northward!

sentences.zh: 蒲口今決千有餘步，迅疾東行，得河舊瀆，行二百里，至歸德橫堤之下，復合正流。

translations.literal: Pukou has now broken for more than a thousand paces; swiftly it runs east, finds the river's old channel, travels two hundred li, reaches below Guide's transverse dike, and rejoins the main current.
translations.idiomatic: At Pukou the breach now spans more than a thousand paces. The current rushes east along the river's old channel for two hundred li, reaches the transverse dike below Guide, and rejoins the main stream.

sentences.zh: 或強湮遏，上決下潰，功不可成。

translations.literal: If one forcibly blocks and restrains it, it will break above and collapse below—the work cannot succeed.
translations.idiomatic: If we forcibly dam it, the river will break out above and collapse below—the work cannot succeed.

sentences.zh: 揆今之計，河北郡縣，順水之性，遠築長垣，以御氾濫；

translations.literal: Considering the plan for today: in Hebei prefectures and counties, follow the water's nature, build long walls far off to ward against flooding;
translations.idiomatic: As I see the policy for today: in the prefectures and counties of Hebei, follow the water's course and build long embankments at a distance to hold back floods;

sentences.zh: 歸德、徐、邳，民避衝潰，聽從安便。

translations.literal: at Guide, Xu, and Pi let the people avoid the rushing breach and be allowed to settle where convenient.
translations.idiomatic: at Guide, Xu, and Pi let the people flee the rushing breach and settle wherever they find safety.

sentences.zh: 被患之家，宜於河南退灘地內，給付頃畝，以為永業；

translations.literal: households afflicted ought within the receded shoals south of the river to be given fields in qing and mu as permanent holdings;
translations.idiomatic: Families stricken by flood should receive allotments of land on the receded shoals south of the river as permanent holdings;

sentences.zh: 異時河決他所者，亦如之。

translations.literal: when hereafter the river breaks elsewhere, let it be the same.
translations.idiomatic: when the river breaks out elsewhere in future, the same policy should apply.

sentences.zh: 信能行此，亦一時救荒之良策也。

translations.literal: If this can truly be carried out, it is also a good policy for relieving famine at one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: If this can truly be implemented, it will also serve as an excellent measure for famine relief in the present crisis.

sentences.zh: 蒲口不塞便。

translations.literal: It is better not to block Pukou.
translations.idiomatic: It is better to leave Pukou unblocked.

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 會河朔郡縣、山東憲部爭言：「不塞則河北桑田盡為魚鱉之區，塞之便。」

translations.literal: But prefectures and counties north of the river and the Shandong Surveillance Commission all contended: "If it is not blocked, all the mulberry fields of Hebei will become a region of fish and turtles—blocking is better."
translations.idiomatic: But officials north of the river and the Shandong Surveillance Commission all argued: "If we do not block it, Hebei's mulberry fields will all become a domain of fish and turtles. Blocking is the better course."

sentences.zh: 帝復從之。

translations.literal: The emperor again followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sided with them.

sentences.zh: 明年，蒲口復決。

translations.literal: The next year Pukou broke again.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Pukou burst again.

sentences.zh: 塞河之役，無歲無之。

translations.literal: The labor of blocking the river—there was no year without it.
translations.idiomatic: River-blocking projects were undertaken every single year.

sentences.zh: 是後水北入复河故道，竟如文言。

translations.literal: After this the water went north and entered the river's old course again, exactly as Wen had said.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the river turned north into its old channel again, exactly as Wen had predicted.

sentences.zh: 三年，調山東憲使，歷行省參知政事、行御史臺中丞。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred as Shandong Surveillance Commissioner, and successively served as Branch Secretariat Vice Administrator and Branch Censorate Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to serve as Shandong Surveillance Commissioner, then held successive posts as Branch Secretariat Vice Administrator and Branch Censorate Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 七年，召拜資善大夫、中書左丞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was summoned and appointed Grand Master for Excellent Goodness and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was summoned and appointed Grand Master for Excellent Goodness and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 浙西飢，發廩不足，募民入粟補官以賑之。

translations.literal: Western Zhe suffered famine; releasing granaries was insufficient, so he recruited the people to contribute grain in exchange for official posts to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: Western Zhe suffered famine. Granary releases were insufficient, so he recruited people to contribute grain in exchange for official appointments as a means of relief.

sentences.zh: 山東歲凶，盜賊竊發，出鈔八百五十餘萬貫以弭之。

translations.literal: Shandong had a bad harvest year; bandits stole forth; he issued more than 8.5 million strings of paper money to quell it.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong had a bad harvest year and banditry broke out. He released more than 8.5 million strings of paper currency to suppress it.

sentences.zh: 選十道使者，奏請巡行天下，問民疾苦。

translations.literal: He selected envoys for ten circuits and memorialized requesting to tour the realm and inquire into the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: He selected envoys for ten circuits and memorialized that they tour the realm to inquire into the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 又奏斥罷南方白雲宗，與民均事賦役。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to dismiss the southern White Cloud sect and make them share corvée and levies with the people.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized to suppress the southern White Cloud sect and subject its members to the same corvée and tax burdens as ordinary people.

sentences.zh: 西域賈人有奉珍寶進售者，其價六十萬錠，省臣平章顧謂文曰：「此所謂押忽大珠也，六十萬酬之不為過矣。」

translations.literal: A Western Regions merchant presented precious objects for sale at a price of 600,000 ingots; a provincial Grand Administrator turned to Wen and said: "This is what is called the yahu great pearl; 600,000 as payment would not be excessive."
translations.idiomatic: A merchant from the Western Regions offered precious goods for sale at a price of 600,000 ingots. A provincial Grand Administrator turned to Wen and said, "This is the so-called yahu great pearl. Six hundred thousand would not be too much to pay."

sentences.zh: 一坐傳玩，文問何所用之，平章曰：「含之可不渴，熨面可使目有光。」

translations.literal: The whole assembly passed it around to admire; Wen asked what use it had; the Grand Administrator said: "Hold it in the mouth and you will not thirst; press it to the face and the eyes will have light."
translations.idiomatic: The whole assembly passed it around in admiration. Wen asked what use it served. The Grand Administrator said, "Hold it in the mouth and you will not thirst; press it to the face and your eyes will shine."

sentences.zh: 文曰：「一人含之，千萬人不渴，則誠寶也；

translations.literal: Wen said: "If one man holds it and ten million men do not thirst, then it is truly a treasure;
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, "If one man could hold it and ten million men would never thirst, then it would truly be a treasure;

sentences.zh: 若一寶止濟一人，則用已微矣。

translations.literal: if one treasure benefits only one man, its use is already slight.
translations.idiomatic: but if one treasure benefits only one man, its usefulness is already slight.

sentences.zh: 吾之所謂寶者，米粟是也，一日不食則飢，三日則疾，七日則死；

translations.literal: What I call a treasure is grain and millet: one day without eating and there is hunger, three days and there is illness, seven days and there is death;
translations.idiomatic: What I call a treasure is grain. One day without food brings hunger, three days bring illness, seven days bring death;

sentences.zh: 有則百姓安，無則天下亂。

translations.literal: with it the hundred clans are at peace, without it the realm is in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: with it the people are secure; without it the realm falls into chaos.

sentences.zh: 以功用較之，豈不愈於彼乎！」

translations.literal: Comparing them by usefulness, is it not better than that!"
translations.idiomatic: Measured by usefulness, is it not far better than that pearl!"

sentences.zh: 平章固請觀之，文竟不為動。

translations.literal: The Grand Administrator insistently asked him to look; Wen in the end was not moved.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Administrator pressed him to look, but Wen would not be moved.

sentences.zh: 年六十九，因疾告老而歸。

translations.literal: At age sixty-nine, because of illness he requested retirement and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At sixty-nine he retired on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜昭文館大學士、中書右丞、商議中書省事，召不起。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Grand Academician of the Hall for Promoting Literature, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Commissioner for Deliberation on Secretariat Affairs; when summoned he did not rise to office.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed Grand Academician of the Hall for Promoting Literature, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Commissioner for Deliberation on Secretariat Affairs, but he did not answer the summons.

sentences.zh: 武宗、仁宗之世，屢延致，訪以國事，賜燕及金帛有加，進階自光祿大夫轉銀青榮祿大夫，仍中書左丞，丐還田裡。

translations.literal: In the reigns of Wuzong and Renzong he was repeatedly invited, consulted on state affairs, granted banquets and increased gifts of gold and silk; he advanced in rank from Grand Master of Splendid Happiness to Grand Master of Silver-Green Glory and Blessing, still Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and begged to return to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wuzong and Renzong he was repeatedly invited, consulted on affairs of state, and honored with banquets and generous gifts of gold and silk. He rose from Grand Master of Splendid Happiness to Grand Master of Silver-Green Glory and Blessing while retaining the post of Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, but begged to return to his home district.

sentences.zh: 延祐六年，拜太子詹事，使三往，乃起。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yanyou he was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; envoys went three times before he rose to office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yanyou he was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent. Envoys were sent three times before he finally accepted.

sentences.zh: 仁宗命盡言以教太子，待以殊禮。

translations.literal: Renzong ordered him to speak fully in instructing the crown prince and treated him with exceptional ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong ordered him to speak freely in instructing the crown prince and treated him with exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 泰定三年，以中書平章政事致仕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiding he retired as Grand Administrator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiding he retired from his post as Grand Administrator of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒於家，年九十二。

translations.literal: The next year he died at home, aged ninety-two.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died at home, aged ninety-two.

sentences.zh: ○申屠致遠

translations.literal: ○ Shen Tuzhiyuan
translations.idiomatic: ○ Shen Tuzhiyuan

sentences.zh: 申屠致遠，字大用，其先汴人。

translations.literal: Shen Tuzhiyuan, styled Dayong, his ancestors were men of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tuzhiyuan, whose courtesy name was Dayong, came from a family originally of Bian.

sentences.zh: 金末從其父義徙居東平之壽張。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jin he followed his father Yi and moved to Shouzhang in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jin dynasty he moved with his father Yi to Shouzhang in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 致遠肄業府學，與李謙、孟祺等齊名。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan studied at the prefectural school and was equally famed with Li Qian, Meng Qi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan studied at the prefectural school and was ranked alongside Li Qian, Meng Qi, and others of equal renown.

sentences.zh: 世祖南征，駐兵小濮，荊湖經略使乞寔力台薦為經略司知事，軍中機務，多所謨畫。

translations.literal: When the Founder campaigned south he stationed troops at Xiao Pu; the Jing-Hu Pacification Commissioner Qishilitai recommended him as director of affairs of the Pacification Office; military affairs he largely planned.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai campaigned south he encamped at Xiao Pu. The Jing-Hu Pacification Commissioner Qishilitai recommended Zhiyuan as director of affairs in the pacification office, and he drafted many of the army's strategic plans.

sentences.zh: 師還，至隨州，所俘男女，致遠悉縱遣之。

translations.literal: When the army returned and reached Suizhou, the men and women taken captive—Zhiyuan released and sent them all away.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned and reached Suizhou, Zhiyuan released all the men and women who had been taken captive.

sentences.zh: 至元七年，崔斌守東平，聘為學官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan Cui Bin guarded Dongping and engaged him as a school officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan, while Cui Bin was defending Dongping, he engaged Zhiyuan as a school officer.

sentences.zh: 十年，御史臺辟為掾，不就，授太常太祝，兼奉禮郎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Censorate recruited him as clerk; he did not accept, and was appointed Grand Sacrificer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, concurrently Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Censorate recruited him as a clerk, but he declined and was appointed Grand Sacrificer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, concurrently Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 帝遣太常卿孛羅問毛血之薦，致遠對曰：「毛以告純，血以告新，禮也。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent Director of Imperial Sacrifices Boluo to ask about offering fur and blood; Zhiyuan replied: "Fur is to report purity, blood is to report freshness—this is ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Director of Imperial Sacrifices Boluo to inquire about the offering of fur and blood. Zhiyuan replied, "Fur announces purity; blood announces freshness. That is ritual propriety."

sentences.zh: 宋平，焦友直、楊居寬宣慰兩浙，舉為都事，首言：「宋圖籍宜上之朝；

translations.literal: When the Song were pacified, Jiao Youzhi and Yang Jukuan as pacification commissioners of the Two Zhes recommended him as chief clerk; his first statement was: "Song maps and registers ought to be submitted to the court;
translations.idiomatic: After the Song were pacified, Jiao Youzhi and Yang Jukuan, serving as pacification commissioners of the Two Zhes, recommended him as chief clerk. His first memorial stated: "The Song maps and registers should be submitted to the court;

sentences.zh: 江南學田，當仍以贍學。」

translations.literal: school fields in Jiangnan ought still to support the schools."
translations.idiomatic: school lands in the south should continue to support education."

sentences.zh: 行省從之。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Branch Secretariat adopted his proposals.

sentences.zh: 轉臨安府安撫司經歷。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be administrator of the Lin'an Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as administrator of the Lin'an Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 臨安改為杭州，遷總管府推官。

translations.literal: When Lin'an was changed to Hangzhou, he was moved to investigating censor of the Metropolitan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin'an was renamed Hangzhou, he was promoted to investigating censor of the metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宋駙馬楊鎮從子玠節，家富於貲，守藏吏姚溶竊其銀，懼事覺，誣玠節陰與宋廣、益二王通，有司榜笞，誣服，獄具。

translations.literal: The Song imperial son-in-law Yang Zhen's nephew Jiejie was wealthy in goods; the keeper of stores Yao Rong stole his silver, feared the matter would be discovered, and falsely accused Jiejie of secretly communicating with the Song Guang and Yi two princes; the authorities beat him with the rod, he confessed under the false charge, and the case was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Jiejie, a nephew of the Song imperial son-in-law Yang Zhen, was a man of great wealth. The storekeeper Yao Rong stole his silver and, fearing discovery, falsely accused Jiejie of secretly communicating with the Song princes Guang and Yi. Officials tortured him until he confessed to the fabricated charge, and the case was closed.

sentences.zh: 致遠讞之，得其情，溶服辜，玠節以賄為謝，致遠怒絕之。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan judged the case, obtained the true circumstances; Rong admitted guilt; Jiejie offered bribes in thanks—Zhiyuan angrily broke off relations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan reviewed the case, uncovered the truth, and Rong confessed his crime. Jiejie tried to thank him with a bribe, but Zhiyuan angrily refused all contact.

sentences.zh: 杭人金淵者，欲冒籍為儒，儒學教授彭宏不從，淵誣宏作詩有異志，揭書於市，邏者以上。

translations.literal: A man of Hangzhou named Jin Yuan wished to falsely register as a scholar; Confucian school instructor Peng Hong would not agree; Yuan falsely accused Hong of composing poetry with rebellious intent, posted the writings in the market, and passers-by reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: A Hangzhou man named Jin Yuan tried to register falsely as a scholar. Confucian school instructor Peng Hong refused. Yuan then accused Hong of writing seditious poetry, posted the writings in the marketplace, and passers-by reported them to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 致遠察其情，執淵窮詰，罪之。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan investigated the circumstances, seized Yuan and questioned him to the end, and punished him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan saw through the scheme, arrested Yuan, interrogated him thoroughly, and punished him.

sentences.zh: 屬縣械反者十七人，訊之，蓋因寇作，以兵自衛，實非反者，皆得釋。

translations.literal: In a subordinate county seventeen men were shackled as rebels; on interrogation it turned out that because bandits had arisen they had taken up arms to defend themselves and were in truth not rebels—all were released.
translations.idiomatic: In a subordinate county seventeen men had been shackled as rebels. On investigation Zhiyuan found that they had armed themselves only to defend against bandits and were not rebels at all. All were released.

sentences.zh: 西僧楊璉真加，作浮圖於宋故宮，欲取高宗所書《九經》石刻以築基，致遠力拒之，乃止。

translations.literal: The Western monk Yang Lianzhenjia built a pagoda in the former Song palace, wishing to take the stone inscriptions of the 《Nine Classics》 written by Emperor Gaozong to build the foundation; Zhiyuan forcefully refused this, and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan monk Yang Lianzhenjia built a pagoda in the former Song palace and wanted to use stone slabs of the 《Nine Classics》 inscribed by Emperor Gaozong as foundation material. Zhiyuan forcefully resisted, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 改壽昌府判官。

translations.literal: He was changed to assistant prefect of Shouchang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as assistant prefect of Shouchang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時寇盜竊發，加​​之造徵日本戰船，遠近騷然，致遠設施有方，眾賴以安。

translations.literal: At the time bandits and robbers broke out in secret, and in addition there was construction to levy war ships for Japan; near and far were disturbed—Zhiyuan deployed measures with method, and the multitude relied on him and were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: At the time bandits were rising throughout the region, and the levy of warships for the campaign against Japan added to the turmoil. Zhiyuan organized relief with wise measures, and the people came to depend on him for security.

sentences.zh: 二十年，拜江南行台監察御史。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed censor of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was appointed censor of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 江淮行省宣使郄顯、李兼訴平章忙兀台不法，有詔勿問，仍以顯等付忙兀台鞫之，係於獄，必抵以死。

translations.literal: Envoys Xi Xian and Li Jian of the Jianghuai Branch Secretariat accused Pacification Commissioner Mamudai of unlawfulness; there was an edict not to inquire, and still Xi and the others were handed to Mamudai to investigate them; they were bound in prison and would certainly be punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Xian and Li Jian, envoys of the Jianghuai Branch Secretariat, accused the Pacification Commissioner Mamudai of misconduct. An edict ordered that the matter not be pursued, yet the complainants were handed over to Mamudai for trial. Imprisoned, they faced certain execution.

sentences.zh: 致遠慮囚浙西，知其冤狀，將縱之，忙兀台脅之以勢，致遠不為動，親脫顯等械，使從軍自贖。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan kept the prisoners in mind in western Zhejiang, knew their wrongful circumstances, and was about to release them; Mamudai threatened him with power—Zhiyuan was not moved, personally removed the shackles of Xi and the others, and had them join the army to redeem themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan, concerned for the prisoners in western Zhejiang, knew they had been wronged and was prepared to release them. Mamudai tried to intimidate him, but Zhiyuan would not be swayed. He personally removed the shackles from Xi and the others and sent them into military service to earn their redemption.

sentences.zh: 桑哥當國，治書侍御史陳天祥使至湖廣，劾平章要束木，桑哥摘其疏中語，誣以不道，奏遣使往訊之，天祥就逮。

translations.literal: Sangge held the state; Associate Drafting Censor Chen Tianxiang was sent to Huguang and impeached Pacification Commissioner Yaosumu; Sangge plucked words from his memorial, falsely charged him with treason, memorialized to send envoys to interrogate him, and Tianxiang was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: While Sangge dominated the government, Associate Drafting Censor Chen Tianxiang was dispatched to Huguang and impeached the Pacification Commissioner Yaosumu. Sangge seized on phrases in Chen's memorial, falsely accused him of treason, and had him arrested for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 時行台遣御史按部湖廣，咸憚之，莫敢往，致遠慨然請行。

translations.literal: At the time the Branch Secretariat sent censors to inspect Huguang; all feared this and none dared go—Zhiyuan ardently volunteered to go.
translations.idiomatic: When the Branch Secretariat dispatched censors to inspect Huguang, everyone feared Sangge's influence and no one dared go. Zhiyuan boldly volunteered for the assignment.

sentences.zh: 比至，累章極論之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he repeatedly memorialized, arguing to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Once there, he submitted memorial after memorial arguing Chen's case with utmost force.

sentences.zh: 桑哥方促定天祥罪，會致遠章上，桑哥氣沮。

translations.literal: Sangge was just pressing to fix Tianxiang's guilt; it happened that Zhiyuan's memorial came up—Sangge's spirit was dispirited.
translations.idiomatic: Sangge was on the verge of securing Chen Tianxiang's conviction when Zhiyuan's memorial reached the throne. Sangge's resolve faltered.

sentences.zh: 江西行省平章馬合謀於商稅外橫加徵取，忽辛籍鄉民為匠戶，轉運使盧世榮榷茶牟利，致遠並劾之。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Ma of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat plotted to levy extractions beyond commercial taxes; Huxin registered village people as artisan households; Transport Commissioner Lu Shirong monopolized tea for profit—Zhiyuan impeached them all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan also impeached the Pacification Commissioner Ma of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat for levying illegal surcharges beyond commercial taxes, Huxin for registering villagers as artisan households, and Transport Commissioner Lu Shirong for profiting from a tea monopoly.

sentences.zh: 又言占城、日本不可涉海遠征，徒費中國；

translations.literal: He also said Champa and Japan could not be reached by distant expedition across the sea—it would vainly waste the Middle Kingdom;
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that distant expeditions by sea against Champa and Japan were impracticable and would merely waste the empire's resources;

sentences.zh: 銓選限以南北，優苦不均，宜考其殿最，量地遠近，定為立制，則銓衡平而吏弊革。

translations.literal: Selection appointments were limited by north and south, favor and hardship were not equal—it was appropriate to examine their best and worst, measure distance of territory, establish fixed regulations, then the balance of selection would be level and official abuses reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments restricted by north-south divisions created unequal hardship; he urged that officials be rated on merit, that posting distances be weighed, and that fixed rules be established so selection would be fair and bureaucratic abuses corrected.

sentences.zh: 他如罷香莎米，弛竹課禁，設司獄官醫學職員，皆致遠發之。

translations.literal: Other matters such as abolishing fragrant sago rice, relaxing bamboo tax prohibitions, and establishing offices for prison officials and medical officers were all initiated by Zhiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Other reforms he proposed included abolishing the fragrant sago rice levy, relaxing bamboo tax restrictions, and establishing posts for prison administrators and medical officers.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，丁父憂，起復江南行台都事，以終制辭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he mourned his father's death; recalled from mourning to be chief administrator of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat—he declined to observe full mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, upon his father's death, he entered mourning. He was recalled to serve as chief administrator of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat but declined, insisting on completing the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，僉江東建康道肅政廉訪司事，未至，移疾還。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed to the Surveillance Commission of Jiankang Circuit in eastern Jiangdong; before arriving he reported illness and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed to the Jiankang Circuit Surveillance Commission in eastern Jiangdong, but before taking up the post he pleaded illness and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，纂修《世祖實錄》，召為翰林待制，不赴。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen, editing the 《Veritable Records of Shizu》, he was summoned as Hanlin Attendant Drafting Scholar—he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yuanzhen era, when the 《Veritable Records of Shizu》 was being compiled, he was summoned to serve as Hanlin Attendant Drafting Scholar but declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 大德二年，僉淮西江北道肅政廉訪司事，行部至和州，得疾卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dade he was appointed to the Surveillance Commission of Huai-West and Jiang-North Circuit; traveling on inspection to Hezhou, he became ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Dade era he was appointed to the Huai-West and Jiang-North Circuit Surveillance Commission. While on inspection in Hezhou he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 致遠清修苦節，恥事權貴，聚書萬卷，名曰墨莊。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan was pure in conduct and bitter in integrity, ashamed to serve the powerful and noble; he gathered ten thousand scrolls of books and called the collection Ink Manor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan was a man of pure conduct and stern integrity who shunned service to the powerful. He amassed a library of ten thousand scrolls, which he called Ink Manor.

sentences.zh: 家無餘產，教諸子如師友。

translations.literal: The household had no surplus property; he taught his sons as teacher and friend.
translations.idiomatic: The family had no surplus wealth; he raised his sons as both teacher and friend.

sentences.zh: 所著《忍齋行稿》四十卷，《釋奠通禮》三卷，《杜詩纂例》十卷，《集驗方》十二卷，《集古印章》三卷。

translations.literal: His writings: 《Collected Manuscripts of the Forbearance Studio》 forty scrolls, 《General Rites for the Sacrifice to Confucius》 three scrolls, 《Collected Examples from Du Fu's Poetry》 ten scrolls, 《Collected Proven Prescriptions》 twelve scrolls, 《Collected Ancient Seals》 three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His works included the forty-scroll 《Collected Manuscripts of the Forbearance Studio》, the three-scroll 《General Rites for the Sacrifice to Confucius》, the ten-scroll 《Collected Examples from Du Fu's Poetry》, the twelve-scroll 《Collected Proven Prescriptions》, and the three-scroll 《Collected Ancient Seals》.

sentences.zh: 子七人：伯騏，徵事郎、嶺北湖南道肅政廉訪司知事；

translations.literal: He had seven sons: Boqi, Attendant Gentleman and administrator of the Surveillance Commission of Lingbei and Hunan Circuit;
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons. The eldest, Boqi, served as Attendant Gentleman and administrator of the Lingbei and Hunan Circuit Surveillance Commission;

sentences.zh: 驥，驪，俱為學官；

translations.literal: Ji and Li both were school officers;
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Li both served as school officers;

sentences.zh: 駉，奉政大夫、兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: Jiong, Grand Master for Governance and Vice Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong held the rank of Grand Master for Governance and served as Vice Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: ○雷膺

translations.literal: ○ Lei Ying
translations.idiomatic: ○ Lei Ying

sentences.zh: 雷膺，字彥正，渾源人。

translations.literal: Lei Ying, courtesy name Yanzheng, was a man of Hunyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Ying, whose courtesy name was Yanzheng, came from Hunyuan.

sentences.zh: 父淵，金監察御史。

translations.literal: His father Yuan was a censor of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan had served as a Jin dynasty censor.

sentences.zh: 膺生七歲而孤，金末，母侯氏挈膺北歸渾源，艱險備嘗，織紝為業，課膺讀書。

translations.literal: Ying at seven sui was orphaned; at the end of Jin, his mother Lady Hou led Ying north back to Hunyuan, experiencing every hardship and danger, took weaving as occupation, and set Ying to read books.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was orphaned at the age of seven. At the end of the Jin dynasty his mother, Lady Hou, took him north to Hunyuan. Enduring every hardship, she supported them by weaving and made him study.

sentences.zh: 膺篤志於學，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Ying was dedicated in will to learning and was known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Ying devoted himself to learning and became known for his filial devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，詔郡國設科選試，凡佔儒籍者復其家，膺年甫弱冠，得與其選，愈自砥礪，遂以文學稱。

translations.literal: In the time of Taizong, an edict ordered the commanderies and states to establish examination selection tests; all who held scholar registration had their households restored—Ying had just reached weak-crown age, obtained participation in the selection, further polished himself, and thus was famed for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Ögedei Khan, an edict ordered regional examinations. Scholar households were exempted from labor service. Ying had just come of age, qualified for the examination, redoubled his efforts, and won a reputation for literary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 丞相史天澤鎮真定，辟為萬戶府掌書記。

translations.literal: Chancellor Shi Tianze garrisoned Zhending and recruited him as chief secretary of the Ten-Thousand Households Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Shi Tianze was stationed at Zhending, he recruited Ying as chief secretary of the Ten-Thousand Households Office.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，初置十路宣撫司，詔選耆舊使副子弟為僚屬，授膺大名路宣撫司員外郎。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, the ten-circuit Pacification Commissions were first established; an edict selected elders' envoys and deputies' sons and younger brothers as staff members—Ying was granted Assistant Director of the Daming Circuit Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After Kublai's accession, when the ten circuit Pacification Commissions were first established, the court ordered that sons of senior officials be selected as staff. Ying was appointed Assistant Director of the Daming Circuit Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，斡林承旨王鶚、王磐薦膺為翰林修撰、同知制誥，兼國史院編修官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong, Hanlin Academy Chancellor Wang E and Wang Pan recommended Ying as Hanlin Compiler, Associate Director of Edicts and Decrees, and concurrently Compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhongtong era, Hanlin Academy Chancellor Wang E and Wang Pan recommended Ying for appointment as Hanlin Compiler, Associate Director of Edicts and Decrees, and concurrent compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 五年，調陝西西蜀四川按察司參議。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Counsellor of the Investigation and Supervision Commission of Shaanxi, Western Shu, and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to serve as counsellor of the Shaanxi, Western Shu, and Sichuan Investigation and Supervision Commission.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，改陝西五路轉運司諮議。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan he was changed to Adviser of the Shaanxi Five-Circuit Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhiyuan era he was reassigned as adviser to the Shaanxi Five-Circuit Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 四年，用兵於蜀，佩金符，參議左壁總帥府事，師還，升承務郎、同知恩州事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, campaigning in Shu, he wore the gold tally, served as counsellor in the Left Wing Commander-in-Chief's headquarters; when the army returned he was promoted to Gentleman for Attending to Affairs and Vice Prefect of Enzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, during the campaign in Shu, he wore an imperial gold tally and served as counsellor on the staff of the Left Wing Commander-in-Chief. When the army returned he was promoted to Gentleman for Attending to Affairs and Vice Prefect of En Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 憲府表薦其能，遂入拜監察御史，首以「正君心、正朝廷百官」為言，又斥聚斂之臣不宜作相。

translations.literal: The Surveillance office memorial-recommended his ability; he then entered and was appointed censor, first speaking on "rectifying the ruler's heart and rectifying the court's hundred officials," and again denouncing revenue-grabbing ministers as unfit to serve as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Surveillance Commission recommended his abilities, and he was appointed censor. His first memorial urged "rectifying the ruler's heart and rectifying the conduct of all court officials," and he also denounced revenue-grabbing ministers as unfit to serve as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 十一年，加奉議大夫，僉河東山西道提刑按察司事，以稱職聞。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was granted Grand Master for Discussion of Governance and appointed to the Penal and Investigation Commission of Hedong and Shanxi; he was known for fulfilling his duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was granted the rank of Grand Master for Discussion of Governance and appointed to the Hedong and Shanxi Penal and Investigation Commission, where he earned a reputation for competent service.

sentences.zh: 十四年，進朝列大夫、山南湖北道提刑按察副使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he advanced to Grand Master of the Court and Vice Commissioner of the Penal and Investigation Commission of Shannan and Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to Grand Master of the Court and appointed Vice Commissioner of the Shannan and Hubei Penal and Investigation Commission.

sentences.zh: 是時，江南新附，諸將市功，且利俘獲，往往濫及無辜，或強籍新民以為奴隸。

translations.literal: At this time the south had newly submitted; generals traded on merit and moreover profited from captives—often extending indiscriminately to the innocent, or forcibly registering new subjects as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the south had only recently submitted. Generals sought credit for military merit and profited from captives, often implicating the innocent or forcibly registering newly submitted subjects as slaves.

sentences.zh: 膺出令，得還為民者以數千計。

translations.literal: Ying issued orders; those who obtained return to commoner status numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Ying issued orders that restored thousands of people to free commoner status.

sentences.zh: 十八年，轉淮西江北道提刑按察副使，以母老辭。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Penal and Investigation Commission of Huai-West and Jiang-North; he declined because his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Huai-West and Jiang-North Penal and Investigation Commission but declined on account of his elderly mother.

sentences.zh: 二十年，遷行台侍御史，奉母之官，分司湖廣、江西，奏劾按察使二人及行省官吏之不法者。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was moved to Palace Censor of the Branch Secretariat, taking his mother to office; he supervised separately in Huguang and Jiangxi, memorializing impeachment of two Investigation Commissioners and unlawful officials of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was promoted to Palace Censor of the Branch Secretariat and brought his mother with him to his post. Operating separately in Huguang and Jiangxi, he impeached two Investigation Commissioners and various corrupt Branch Secretariat officials.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，丁母憂，去官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he mourned his mother's death and left office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, upon his mother's death, he left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 明年，起復，授中議大夫、江南浙西道提刑按察使。

translations.literal: The next year, recalled from mourning, he was granted Grand Master for Discussing Governance and appointed Commissioner of the Penal and Investigation Commission of Jiangnan and Western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled from mourning and appointed Grand Master for Discussing Governance and Commissioner of the Jiangnan and Western Zhejiang Penal and Investigation Commission.

sentences.zh: 時蘇、湖多雨傷稼，百姓艱食，膺請於朝，發廩米二十萬石賑之。

translations.literal: At the time Suzhou and Huzhou had much rain damaging the crops; the common people had difficult food—Ying requested of the court to release two hundred thousand shi of granary rice to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains around Suzhou and Huzhou had damaged the harvest, and the people were going hungry. Ying petitioned the court to release two hundred thousand shi of granary rice for relief.

sentences.zh: 江淮行省以發米太多，議存三之一，膺曰：「布宣皇澤，惠養困窮，行省臣職耳，豈可效有司出納之吝耶！」

translations.literal: The Jianghuai Branch Secretariat, because the rice released was too much, deliberated keeping one-third; Ying said: "To spread the imperial grace and nurture the struggling and destitute is the duty of Branch Secretariat ministers—how can one imitate the stinginess of ordinary officials in receipts and disbursements!"
translations.idiomatic: The Jianghuai Branch Secretariat, thinking the amount excessive, proposed retaining only one-third. Ying said, "To spread the emperor's benevolence and succor the destitute is the duty of Branch Secretariat officials. How can we imitate the petty stinginess of clerks counting receipts and disbursements!"

sentences.zh: 行省不能奪，悉給之。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat could not override him and gave it all.
translations.idiomatic: The Branch Secretariat could not overturn his decision, and the full amount was distributed.

sentences.zh: 時年六十二，即致仕，歸老於山陽。

translations.literal: At the time he was sixty-two sui; he immediately retired and returned to old age at Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of sixty-two he retired and spent his old age at Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，徵拜集賢學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was summoned and appointed Academic Scholar of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was summoned and appointed Academic Scholar of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 成宗即位，朝會上都，召諸故老，諮詢國政，膺為稱首，多所建白。

translations.literal: When Chengzong took the throne, at court assembly at Shangdu the former elders were summoned and consulted on state affairs—Ying was foremost and made many proposals.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong ascended the throne, he held court at Shangdu and summoned former senior officials to advise on state affairs. Ying was chief among them and offered many recommendations.

sentences.zh: 一日，延見便殿，奏對稱旨，賜白玉帶環一。

translations.literal: One day he was received in audience in the side hall; his memorial replies matched the emperor's intent, and he was granted one white jade belt ring.
translations.idiomatic: One day he was received in audience in the side hall. His responses pleased the emperor, who bestowed on him a white jade belt clasp.

sentences.zh: 明年，賜鈔五千貫，進秩二品。

translations.literal: The next year he was granted five thousand guan of paper currency and advanced in rank to second grade.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was granted five thousand guan in paper currency and promoted to second rank.

sentences.zh: 大德元年夏六月，以疾卒於京師，年七十三。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer in the first year of Dade he died of illness in the capital; he was seventy-three sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer in the first year of the Dade era he died of illness in the capital at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 贈通奉大夫、河南江北等處行中書省參知政事、護軍，追封馮翊郡公，諡文穆。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Master for Promoting Governance, Vice Administrator of the Branch Secretariat for Henan and Jiang-North and Other Regions, and Defender of the Army; retroactively enfeoffed as Duke of Fengyi Commandery with posthumous title Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the rank of Master for Promoting Governance, Vice Administrator of the Henan and Jiang-North Branch Secretariat, and Defender of the Army, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Fengyi Commandery with the posthumous title Wenmu.

sentences.zh: 子肇，順德路總管府判官。

translations.literal: His son Zhao was Assistant Administrator of the Zhende Circuit Metropolitan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao served as Assistant Administrator of the Zhende Circuit Metropolitan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 孫豫，南陽府穰縣尹。

translations.literal: His grandson Yu was magistrate of Xiang County in Nanyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yu served as magistrate of Xiang County in Nanyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: ○胡祗皞

translations.literal: ○ Hu Zhiyuan
translations.idiomatic: ○ Hu Zhiyuan

sentences.zh: 胡祗遹，字紹聞，磁州武安人。

translations.literal: Hu Zhiyuan, courtesy name Shaowen, was a man of Wu'an in Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhiyuan, whose courtesy name was Shaowen, came from Wu'an in Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，既長讀書，見知於名流。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, when grown he read books and was recognized by eminent figures.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned as a youth, he devoted himself to study and won recognition among leading scholars.

sentences.zh: 中統初，張文謙宣撫大名，辟員外郎。

translations.literal: In the early Zhongtong era, Zhang Wenqian pacified Daming and recruited him as Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhongtong era, when Zhang Wenqian served as pacification commissioner of Daming, he recruited Hu as Assistant Director.

sentences.zh: 明年，入為中書詳定官。

translations.literal: The next year he entered to serve as Detailed Review Officer in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he entered central service as Detailed Review Officer in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，授應奉翰林文字，尋兼太常博士，調戶部員外郎，轉右司員外郎，尋兼左司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan he was granted Hanlin Attendant for Drafts, soon also Grand Master of Ceremonial; transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, moved to Vice Director in the Right Secretariat, soon also the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhiyuan era he was appointed Hanlin Attendant for Drafts, then concurrently Grand Master of Ceremonial. He was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, then to Vice Director in the Right Secretariat, and soon served concurrently in the Left Secretariat as well.

sentences.zh: 時阿合馬當國，進用群下，官冗事煩，祗遹建言：「省官莫如省吏，省吏莫如省事。」

translations.literal: At the time Ahmad held the state, advancing and employing many subordinates; offices were redundant and affairs numerous—Zhiyuan submitted advice: "To reduce officials, nothing is better than reducing clerks; to reduce clerks, nothing is better than reducing affairs."
translations.idiomatic: While Ahmad dominated the government and packed offices with his followers, bureaucratic workload grew unbearable. Hu Zhiyuan submitted a memorial: "The best way to reduce officials is to reduce clerks; the best way to reduce clerks is to reduce unnecessary business."

sentences.zh: 以是忤權奸，出為太原路治中，兼提舉本路鐵冶，將以歲賦不辦責之。

translations.literal: Because of this he offended the powerful villain and was sent out as Vice Administrator of Taiyuan Circuit, concurrently Supervisor of Iron Smelting of this circuit—they intended to hold him responsible for failure to complete the annual levy.
translations.idiomatic: This offended the powerful faction, and he was sent out to serve as Vice Administrator of Taiyuan Circuit while also supervising the circuit's iron smelting. His enemies intended to blame him if the annual levy fell short.

sentences.zh: 及其蒞職，乃以最聞。

translations.literal: When he arrived at his post, he was instead famed for excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took up the post, he distinguished himself as the circuit's most capable administrator.

sentences.zh: 改河東山西道提刑按察副使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Commissioner of the Penal and Investigation Commission of Hedong and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as Vice Commissioner of the Hedong and Shanxi Penal and Investigation Commission.

sentences.zh: 宋平，為荊湖北道宣慰副使。

translations.literal: When Song was pacified, he served as Vice Pacification Commissioner of Jinghu North Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of the Song, he served as Vice Pacification Commissioner of the Jinghu North Circuit.

sentences.zh: 有佃民訴其田主謀為不軌者，祗遹察其冤，坐告者。

translations.literal: There was a tenant who accused his landlord of plotting sedition—Zhiyuan investigated and found him wronged; he punished the accuser.
translations.idiomatic: When a tenant accused his landlord of plotting rebellion, Hu Zhiyuan found the charge false and punished the accuser.

sentences.zh: 十九年，為濟寧路總管，上八事於樞府言軍政：曰役重，曰逃戶，曰貧難，曰正身入役，曰偽署文牒，曰官吏保結，曰有名無實，曰合併偏頗。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was Metropolitan Prefect of Jining Circuit; he submitted eight matters to the Military Affairs Commission on military administration: saying corvée was heavy, saying fleeing households, saying poverty hardship, saying personal service, saying forged documents, saying officials' surety bonds, saying names without substance, saying merged partiality.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he served as Metropolitan Prefect of Jining Circuit and submitted eight proposals on military administration to the Military Affairs Commission: burdensome corvée, fleeing households, poverty and hardship, personal conscription, forged documents, officials' surety bonds, nominal units with no real force, and uneven consolidation of units.

sentences.zh: 樞府是之，以其言著為定法。

translations.literal: The Military Affairs Commission approved them and made his words fixed law.
translations.idiomatic: The Military Affairs Commission approved his proposals and codified them as permanent regulations.

sentences.zh: 濟寧移治鉅野縣，自國初經兵戈，其廢已久，民居未集，風俗樸野。

translations.literal: Jining moved its seat to Juye County; since the founding of the state it had passed through warfare and weapons—its abandonment had long been so; common people dwellings were not gathered, customs were plain and wild.
translations.idiomatic: Jining's administrative seat was moved to Juye County, which had lain in ruins since the wars at the dynasty's founding. The population had not yet recovered, and local customs remained rough and uncultivated.

sentences.zh: 祗遹選郡子弟，擇師教之，親為講論，期變其俗，久之，治效以最稱。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan selected the circuit's young men, chose teachers to instruct them, personally lectured and discussed, expecting to change their customs; after long time, his governing effectiveness was famed as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhiyuan selected local youths, appointed teachers, and personally lectured them in the hope of reforming local customs. In time his administration was rated the best in the region.

sentences.zh: 升山東東西道提刑按察使，所至抑豪右，扶寡弱，以敦教化，以厲士風。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Penal and Investigation Commission of Shandong East and West; wherever he went he suppressed powerful families, supported the orphaned and weak, to promote instruction and transformation, to sharpen scholar fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Commissioner of the Shandong East and West Penal and Investigation Commission, he suppressed powerful local families, aided the weak, promoted education, and strengthened scholarly standards wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 民有父子兄弟相訟者，必懇切諭以天倫之重，不獲已，則繩以法。

translations.literal: When common people had fathers and sons or brothers suing one another, he always earnestly admonished them on the weight of human relations—only when they could not be helped did he bind them with law.
translations.idiomatic: When fathers and sons or brothers sued one another, he always earnestly appealed to the bonds of family duty. Only when persuasion failed did he punish them according to law.

sentences.zh: 召拜翰林學士，不赴，改江南浙西道提刑按察使，未幾，以疾歸。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Hanlin Academy Scholar—he did not go; changed to Commissioner of the Penal and Investigation Commission of Jiangnan and Western Zhejiang; before long, on account of illness he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to serve as Hanlin Academy Scholar, he declined. He was instead appointed Commissioner of the Jiangnan and Western Zhejiang Penal and Investigation Commission but soon retired on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，朝廷徵耆德者十人，祗遹為之首，以疾辭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the court summoned ten elders of virtue—Zhiyuan was first among them; he declined on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year the court summoned ten venerable scholars of virtue. Hu Zhiyuan headed the list but declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 三十年，卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he died; he was sixty-seven sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he died at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 延祐年，贈禮部尚書，諡文靖。

translations.literal: In the Yanyou years he was posthumously granted Minister of Rites with posthumous title Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yanyou era he was posthumously granted the title Minister of Rites with the posthumous name Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 子持，太常博士。

translations.literal: His son Chi was Grand Master of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chi served as Grand Master of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: ○王利用

translations.literal: ○ Wang Liyong
translations.idiomatic: ○ Wang Liyong

sentences.zh: 王利用，字國賓，通州潞縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Liyong, courtesy name Guobin, was a man of Lu County in Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liyong, whose courtesy name was Guobin, came from Lu County in Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 遼贈中書令、太原郡公籍之七世孫，高祖以下皆仕金。

translations.literal: Seventh-generation descendant of Ji, posthumously granted Secretariat Director and Duke of Taiyuan Commandery in Liao; from great-great-grandfather down all served Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was the seventh-generation descendant of Ji, who had been posthumously granted Secretariat Director and enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan Commandery under the Liao. From his great-great-grandfather onward, his forebears had all served the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 利用幼穎悟，弱冠與魏初同學，遂齊名，諸名公交口稱譽之。

translations.literal: Liyong was quick-witted in youth; at weak crown he studied with Wei Chu and then shared equal fame—the various eminent men all praised him with one voice.
translations.idiomatic: Liyong was unusually bright as a boy. When he came of age he studied with Wei Chu, and the two quickly won equal renown. Leading scholars competed to praise them.

sentences.zh: 初事世祖於潛邸，中書辟為掾，辭不就。

translations.literal: He first served Shizu at the Hidden Residence; the Secretariat recruited him as clerk—he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Kublai while the future emperor was still heir apparent. The Secretariat recruited him as a clerk, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 中統初，命監鑄百司印章，歷太府內藏官，出為山東經略司詳議官，遷北京奧魯同知，歷安肅、汝、蠡、趙四州知州，入拜監察御史。

translations.literal: In the early Zhongtong era he was ordered to supervise casting seals for the hundred offices; passed through Grand Capital Inner Storehouse officer; sent out as Detailed Review Officer of the Shandong Pacification Commission; moved to Vice Administrator of the Beijing Aurora; served successively as prefect of Ansu, Ru, Li, and Zhao—the four prefectures; entered and was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhongtong era he was charged with supervising the casting of seals for the various offices. He served as an officer in the Grand Capital Inner Storehouse, then as Detailed Review Officer on the Shandong Pacification Commission staff, Vice Administrator of the Beijing garrison command, and successively as prefect of Ansu, Ru, Li, and Zhao before being appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 薊州有禁地，民不得射獵其中，邏者誣州民冒禁，籍其家，利用糾之，邏者訴於上，利用辨愈力，得以所沒入悉歸之民。

translations.literal: Jizhou had forbidden land—common people could not hunt within it; patrol officers falsely accused prefecture people of trespassing the prohibition, registered their households; Liyong corrected this—the patrol officers appealed upward; Liyong argued more forcefully, and obtained that all confiscated goods were wholly returned to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhou had a prohibited hunting ground, and a patrol officer falsely accused local residents of trespassing and confiscated their property. Liyong investigated the case. When the patrol officer appealed to the court, Liyong argued all the more forcefully, and the confiscated goods were fully restored to the people.

sentences.zh: 擢翰林待制，兼興文署，奉旨程試上都、隆興等路儒士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin Attendant Drafting Scholar, concurrently serving the Office for the Promotion of Literature; by imperial order he examined by schedule the scholars of Shangdu, Longxing, and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin Attendant Drafting Scholar and concurrently served in the Office for the Promotion of Literature. By imperial order he conducted examinations of scholars in Shangdu, Longxing, and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 升直學士，與耶律鑄同修實錄。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Direct Academy Scholar; with Yelü Zhu he jointly compiled the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Direct Academy Scholar, he collaborated with Yelü Zhu on compiling the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 出為河東、陝西、燕南三道提刑按察副使、四川提刑按察使。

translations.literal: Sent out as Vice Commissioner of the Penal and Investigation Commissions of Hedong, Shaanxi, and Yannan, and Commissioner of the Sichuan Penal and Investigation Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve concurrently as Vice Commissioner of the Hedong, Shaanxi, and Yannan Penal and Investigation Commissions and as Commissioner of the Sichuan Penal and Investigation Commission.

sentences.zh: 四川土豪有持官府長短者，問得其實，而當以罪，民賴以安。

translations.literal: In Sichuan local strongmen who held the government offices' faults and virtues—in questioning he obtained the truth, and they were properly punished with crime; the people relied on this and were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: In Sichuan, when powerful local families tried to hold officials hostage, he investigated thoroughly, punished the guilty, and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 都元帥塔海，抑巫山縣民數百口為奴，民屢訴不決，利用承檄核問，盡出為民。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Tahai oppressed several hundred mouths of Wushan County people as slaves; the people repeatedly appealed without resolution—Liyong received the order and examined the question, and all were released as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The Commander-in-Chief Tahai had forced several hundred residents of Wushan County into slavery. Repeated appeals had gone unresolved until Liyong was ordered to investigate and restored them all to free status.

sentences.zh: 大德二年，改安西、興元兩路總管。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dade he was changed to Metropolitan Prefect of the two circuits of Anxi and Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Dade era he was reassigned as Metropolitan Prefect of the Anxi and Xingyuan circuits.

sentences.zh: 其在興元，減職田租額，站戶之役於他郡者悉除之，民甚便焉。

translations.literal: When he was at Xingyuan, he reduced the official-field rent quota; station households serving corvée in other commanderies were all exempted—the people were greatly benefited.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingyuan he reduced the rents on official fields and exempted station households from corvée service in other jurisdictions. The people found the relief greatly beneficial.

sentences.zh: 有婦毒殺其夫，問藥所從來，吏教婦指為富商所貨。

translations.literal: There was a woman who poisoned and killed her husband; when asked where the medicine came from, clerks taught the woman to point to a wealthy merchant as the seller.
translations.idiomatic: When a woman poisoned her husband, clerks coached her to claim she had bought the poison from a wealthy merchant.

sentences.zh: 獄上，利用曰：「家富而貨毒藥，豈人情哉？」

translations.literal: When the case went up, Liyong said: "A family rich yet selling poison medicine—how is this human feeling?"
translations.idiomatic: When the case came before him, Liyong said, "Would a wealthy family really sell poison? That defies common sense."

sentences.zh: 訊之，果冤也。

translations.literal: On interrogation, it was indeed a false charge.
translations.idiomatic: On re-examination, the merchant was indeed innocent.

sentences.zh: 未幾，致仕，居漢中。

translations.literal: Before long he retired and dwelt at Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he retired and lived in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 成宗朝，起為太子賓客，首以切於時政者疏上十七事：曰謹畏天戒，取法祖宗，孝事母后，敬奉至尊，撫愛百姓，敦本抑末，清心聽政，寡欲養身，酒宜節飲，財宜節用，有功必賞，有罪必罰，杜絕讒言，求納直諫，官職量材而授，工役相時而動，俾近侍時赴經筵講讀經史。

translations.literal: In the Chengzong reign he was raised as Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; first he memorialized seventeen matters cutting close to current politics: saying reverently fear heavenly warnings, take law from the ancestral founders, filially serve the empress dowager, respectfully serve the supreme sovereign, soothe and love the hundred surname, promote root and suppress branch, purify the heart and listen to government, few desires and nurture the body, wine should be drunk in moderation, wealth should be spent in moderation, merit must be rewarded, crime must be punished, cut off slanderous words, seek and accept straight remonstrance, official posts measure talent and then grant, labor projects observe the season and then move, cause attendants at times to attend the Classic Lectern to lecture and read the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Chengzong he was recalled to serve as Preceptor of the Heir Apparent. He submitted a memorial listing seventeen urgent recommendations on current policy: reverently heed Heaven's warnings, take the founding emperors as models, serve the empress dowager with filial devotion, honor the sovereign, cherish the people, promote agriculture and restrain commerce, govern with a clear mind, live simply, drink in moderation, spend sparingly, reward merit and punish crime, shut out slander, welcome frank counsel, appoint officials according to talent, launch public works at proper seasons, and require attendants to attend regular lectures on the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 帝及太子嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor and the heir apparent praised and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and the heir apparent praised and accepted his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 皇后聞之，命錄別本以進。

translations.literal: The empress heard of it and ordered a separate copy recorded and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress heard of this, she ordered a separate copy made and submitted to the court.

sentences.zh: 利用以老病不能朝，帝遣醫診視之，利用謂弟利貞、利亨曰：「吾受國厚恩，愧不能報，死生有命，藥不能為也。」

translations.literal: Because Liyong was aged and ill and could not attend court, the emperor sent physicians to examine him; Liyong told his younger brothers Lizhen and Liheng: "I have received thick grace from the state and am ashamed that I cannot repay it; life and death are fated—medicine cannot help."
translations.idiomatic: Liyong's age and illness kept him from court, so the emperor sent physicians to examine him. He told his younger brothers Lizhen and Liheng, "The state has shown me great favor, and I am ashamed that I cannot repay it. Life and death are ordained; medicine can do nothing."

sentences.zh: 遂卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: He then died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He then died, at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 利用每自言，平生讀書，於恕字有得焉。
