translations.literal: Liyong often said of himself that in reading all his life he had gained something in the character for forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Liyong often said that of all he had read in his life, he had gained most from the virtue of forbearance.

sentences.zh: 廉希憲當時名相，簡重慎許可，嘗語人曰：「方今文章政事兼備者，王國賓其人也。」

translations.literal: Lian Xixian, a famous chancellor of the time, grave and restrained in granting praise, once told people: "Among those today who combine literary and administrative excellence, Wang Guobin is the man."
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian, then a celebrated chancellor, was sparing and solemn in praise. He once said, "Of those today who unite literary talent with administrative skill, Wang Guobin is the man."

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，以官僚舊臣，制贈榮祿大夫、柱國、中書平章政事，封潞國公，諡文貞。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, as an old bureaucrat and veteran minister, by decree he was posthumously granted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of the State, and Central Secretariat Associate Grand Councillor, enfeoffed Duke of Lu State, posthumous name Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong ascended the throne, Liyong was posthumously honored as an old servant of the bureaucracy: Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of the State, and Associate Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Lu State with the posthumous name Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: ○暢師文

translations.literal: ○ Chang Shiwen
translations.idiomatic: ○ Chang Shiwen

sentences.zh: 暢師文，字純甫，南陽人。

translations.literal: Chang Shiwen, courtesy name Chunfu, was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Shiwen, whose courtesy name was Chunfu, came from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖淵，贈中順大夫、上騎都尉、魏郡伯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuan was posthumously granted Grand Master for Ordered Fidelity, Chief Cavalry Commandant of the Upper Rank, and Baron of Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuan was posthumously granted the rank of Grand Master for Ordered Fidelity and Chief Cavalry Commandant of the Upper Rank and was enfeoffed as Baron of Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父訥，有詩名，注《地理指掌圖》，仕為汴幕官，贈太中大夫、上輕車都尉、魏郡侯。

translations.literal: His father Ne had a reputation in poetry, annotated the 《Geographical Handbook Map》, served as a secretariat officer at Bian, and was posthumously granted Grand Master for Grand Harmony, Light Chariot Commandant of the Upper Rank, and Marquis of Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ne was known for poetry, annotated the 《Geographical Handbook Map》, and served as a secretariat officer at Bian. He was posthumously granted the rank of Grand Master for Grand Harmony and Light Chariot Commandant of the Upper Rank and enfeoffed as Marquis of Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 師文幼警悟，家貧無書，手錄口誦，過目輒不忘。

translations.literal: Shiwen was precocious in youth; the family was poor and had no books; he copied by hand and recited aloud, and what passed before his eyes he never forgot.
translations.idiomatic: Shiwen was unusually bright as a boy. The family was poor and owned no books, so he copied texts by hand and recited them aloud; whatever he glanced at once stayed in memory.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，謁許衡，與衡門人姚燧、高凝皆相友善。

translations.literal: At weak crown he visited Xu Heng; with Xu's disciples Yao Sui and Gao Ning he was on friendly terms.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he visited Xu Heng and became close friends with Xu's disciples Yao Sui and Gao Ning.

sentences.zh: 至元五年，陳時政十六策，丞相安童奇其才，辟為右三部令史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhiyuan he submitted sixteen policies on current affairs; Chancellor Antong marveled at his talent and recruited him as clerk of the Right Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Zhiyuan reign he submitted sixteen proposals on current affairs. Chancellor Antong was struck by his ability and recruited him as a clerk in the Right Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 十二年，丞相伯顏攻宋，選為掾屬，從定江南，及歸，舟中惟載書籍而已。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Chancellor Bayan attacked Song; he was selected as a staff member, followed in pacifying Jiangnan, and on his return his boat carried only books.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, when Chancellor Bayan attacked the Song, he was chosen as a staff officer and followed the campaign to pacify Jiangnan. On the voyage home his boat held nothing but books.

sentences.zh: 十三年，編《平宋事蹟》上之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he compiled the 《Records of the Pacification of Song》 and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he compiled the 《Records of the Pacification of Song》 and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 十四年，除東川行樞密院都事，盡心贊畫，多所裨益。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Chief of the Eastern Sichuan Branch Secretariat for Military Affairs; he devoted himself to planning and contributed much.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was appointed chief of staff at the Eastern Sichuan Branch Secretariat for Military Affairs, where he threw himself into planning and rendered substantial service.

sentences.zh: 十六年，安西王承製改四川北道宣慰司經歷，尋除承直郎、潼川路治中。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Prince Anxi by provisional order changed him to Administrative Officer of the Northern Sichuan Circuit Pacification Commission; soon he was appointed Gentleman for Upholding Integrity and Vice Prefect of Tongchuan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Prince Anxi provisionally transferred him to administrative officer of the Northern Sichuan Circuit Pacification Commission. He was soon appointed Gentleman for Upholding Integrity and Vice Prefect of Tongchuan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 修府舍，發地得銀五十錠，同僚分師文十錠，不受，用以修廟學及傳舍，餘作酒器給公用。

translations.literal: When renovating the official residence, excavating the ground yielded fifty ingots of silver; colleagues allotted Shiwen ten ingots—he refused; he used the silver to repair the temple school and relay station, and made the remainder into wine vessels for public use.
translations.idiomatic: While renovating the official residence, workers unearthed fifty ingots of silver. His colleagues offered Shiwen ten ingots, but he refused them. He used the silver to repair the temple school and the relay station and had the remainder made into wine vessels for public use.

sentences.zh: 十九年，承製改同知保寧路事，治尚平簡，反側以安。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year by provisional order he was changed to Vice Administrator of Baoning Circuit; his governance favored fairness and simplicity, and the restive were thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was provisionally appointed Vice Administrator of Baoning Circuit. His administration was fair and unpretentious, and the unsettled were calmed.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，僉西蜀四川道提刑按察司事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed Associate Commissioner of the Sichuan Circuit Penal and Investigation Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was appointed Associate Commissioner of the Sichuan Circuit Penal and Investigation Commission.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，拜監察御史，糾劾不避權貴，上所纂《農桑輯要》書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was appointed censor; in impeaching he did not avoid the powerful and noble, and presented the emperor's compiled book the 《Essentials of Agriculture and Sericulture》.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was appointed censor. He impeached without sparing the powerful, and presented the emperor's compiled work, the 《Essentials of Agriculture and Sericulture》.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，遷陝西漢中道巡行勸農副使，置義倉，教民種藝法。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was moved to Vice Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture of the Shaanxi-Hanzhong Circuit; he established charity granaries and taught the people methods of planting.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Vice Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture on the Shaanxi-Hanzhong Circuit. He established charity granaries and taught the people improved farming methods.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，改僉陝西漢中道提刑按察司事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was changed to Associate Commissioner of the Shaanxi-Hanzhong Circuit Penal and Investigation Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was transferred to Associate Commissioner of the Shaanxi-Hanzhong Circuit Penal and Investigation Commission.

sentences.zh: 時更提刑按察司為肅政廉訪司，就僉本道肅政廉訪司事，黜姦舉才，咸服其公。

translations.literal: At the time the Penal and Investigation Commission was changed to the Commission for Purging Corruption and Investigating Misconduct; he was appointed Associate Commissioner of this circuit's commission; he dismissed the wicked and promoted talent, and all submitted to his fairness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Penal and Investigation Commission was reorganized as the Commission for Purging Corruption and Investigating Misconduct, he was appointed its associate commissioner for the circuit. He removed the corrupt and advanced the able, and all acknowledged his fairness.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，徙山南道。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was transferred to the Southern Mountains Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was transferred to the Southern Mountains Circuit.

sentences.zh: 松滋、枝江有水患，歲發民防水，往返數百里，苦於供給，師文以江水安流，悉罷其役。

translations.literal: Songzi and Zhijiang had water disasters; each year people were conscripted to guard against flood, traveling back and forth several hundred li and suffering from supply; Shiwen, because the river water flowed peacefully, completely abolished the corvee.
translations.idiomatic: Songzi and Zhijiang suffered from flooding. Each year the people were conscripted for flood control, traveling hundreds of li back and forth at great cost in supplies. Shiwen saw that the river had settled, and abolished the labor entirely.

sentences.zh: 駙馬亦都護家人怙勢不法，師文治其甚惡者，流之。

translations.literal: Members of the household of Imperial Son-in-law Yidu Hu relied on power and violated the law; Shiwen punished the worst offenders and banished them.
translations.idiomatic: Members of Imperial Son-in-law Yidu Hu's household relied on their patron's power to break the law. Shiwen punished the worst offenders and had them banished.

sentences.zh: 大德二年，改山東道，入為國子司業。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dade he was transferred to the Shandong Circuit and entered the capital as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Dade reign he was transferred to the Shandong Circuit, then recalled to the capital as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 七年，出為陝西行中書省理問官，決滯獄，不少阿徇。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was sent out as judicial inquirer of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat; he decided stagnant cases without favoring anyone.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was sent out as judicial inquirer of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat. He cleared backlogged cases without showing favor to anyone.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以疾家居。

translations.literal: Before long, because of illness he remained at home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long illness forced him to retire to his home.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢陝西漢中道肅政廉訪副使，又以疾不赴。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to Vice Surveillance Commissioner of the Shaanxi-Hanzhong Circuit for Purging Corruption, but again because of illness did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to Vice Surveillance Commissioner of the Shaanxi-Hanzhong Circuit for Purging Corruption, but illness again kept him from taking office.

sentences.zh: 十年，改太常少卿，轉翰林侍讀學士、朝請大夫、知制誥同修國史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was changed to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then transferred to Hanlin Attendant Reader, Grand Master for Court Appearances, Drafting Officer, and Joint Compiler of National History.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then transferred to Hanlin Attendant Reader with the ranks of Grand Master for Court Appearances, Drafting Officer, and Joint Compiler of National History.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，修《成宗實錄》，賜鈔壹百錠，不受。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida he edited the 《Veritable Records of Chengzong》; he was granted one hundred ingots of paper money and did not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhida reign he helped compile the 《Veritable Records of Chengzong》. He was granted one hundred ingots of paper money but refused them.

sentences.zh: 時製作多出其手。

translations.literal: At the time many compositions came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many court compositions came from his hand.

sentences.zh: 二年，加少中大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to Junior Middle Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to Junior Middle Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 三年，請補外任，除太平路總管。

translations.literal: In the third year he requested an outside appointment and was appointed Chief Administrator of Taiping Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he asked for a provincial post and was appointed Chief Administrator of Taiping Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時大旱，師文捐俸致禱，不數日，澍雨大降，遂為豐年。

translations.literal: At the time there was great drought; Shiwen donated his salary to pray for rain; within days timely rain fell heavily, and the year became abundant.
translations.idiomatic: A severe drought gripped the region. Shiwen donated his salary to pray for rain, and within days a soaking rain fell; the year turned abundant.

sentences.zh: 當塗人坐殺牛祈雨，囚系者六十餘人，師文憫而出之。

translations.literal: People of Dangtu who had killed cattle to pray for rain—more than sixty were imprisoned; Shiwen took pity on them and released them.
translations.idiomatic: More than sixty people of Dangtu who had slaughtered cattle to pray for rain were imprisoned. Shiwen took pity on them and set them free.

sentences.zh: 公田米積之盈屋，曰：「我家幾人，能盡食此乎！」

translations.literal: Public-field rice piled up filling the house; he said: "How many are there in my household—can we eat all this!"
translations.idiomatic: Rice from the public fields piled up until it filled the house. He said, "There are only a few of us at home—how could we ever eat all this!"

sentences.zh: 呼貧士及細民，恣其取去。

translations.literal: He called poor scholars and common people and let them take freely.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned poor scholars and common people and let them take as much as they wished.

sentences.zh: 廉訪分司官前後至者，必先謁師文，稱為先生。

translations.literal: Surveillance sub-commission officials who came before and after always first visited Shiwen and called him Master.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance sub-commission officials who arrived in succession always paid their first visit to Shiwen and addressed him as Master.

sentences.zh: 師文在任未久，境內晏然。

translations.literal: Shiwen had not long been in office, yet within the jurisdiction all was peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shiwen had been in office only a short time, the circuit was entirely at peace.

sentences.zh: 皇慶二年，復召為翰林侍讀學士、中奉大夫、知制誥同修國史，奉旨撰《王勃成道記序》等文，賜銀貳鋌，不受。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangqing he was again recalled as Hanlin Attendant Reader, Grand Master for Attending the Court, Drafting Officer, and Joint Compiler of National History; by imperial order he composed texts such as the 《Preface to the Record of Wang Bo's Attainment of the Way》; he was granted two ingots of silver and did not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Huangqing reign he was recalled as Hanlin Attendant Reader with the ranks of Grand Master for Attending the Court, Drafting Officer, and Joint Compiler of National History. By imperial order he wrote pieces including the 《Preface to the Record of Wang Bo's Attainment of the Way》. He was granted two ingots of silver but refused them.

sentences.zh: 除燕南河北道肅政廉訪使，以病去官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of the Yannan-Hebei Circuit for Purging Corruption and left office because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of the Yannan-Hebei Circuit for Purging Corruption but resigned because of illness.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，徵拜翰林學士、資德大夫，行至河南，復以病歸襄陽。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou he was summoned as Hanlin Academician and Grand Master for Cherishing Virtue; reaching Henan, he again returned to Xiangyang because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yanyou reign he was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician and Grand Master for Cherishing Virtue. When he reached Henan, illness forced him to return to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 四年秋八月，考河南鄉試歸，次襄縣，卒於傳舍，年七十一，葬襄陽峴山。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn in the fourth year, after examining the Henan provincial examination he returned; stopping at Xiang County, he died at a relay station, aged seventy-one, and was buried at Xian Mountain in Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn in the fourth year, while returning from supervising the Henan provincial examination, he stopped at Xiang County and died at a relay station. He was seventy-one and was buried on Xian Mountain in Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 泰定二年，贈資政大夫、河南江北等處行中書省左丞、上護軍，追封魏郡公，諡文肅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiding he was posthumously granted Grand Master for Assisting Governance, Left Assistant Administrator of the Henan-Jiangbei Branch Secretariat, and Chief Guard General of the Upper Rank; posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Wei Commandery; posthumous name Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Taiding reign he was posthumously granted the rank of Grand Master for Assisting Governance and Chief Guard General of the Upper Rank and appointed Left Assistant Administrator of the Henan-Jiangbei Branch Secretariat. He was enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Wei Commandery with the posthumous name Wensu.

sentences.zh: 後至元八年，加贈推忠守正亮節功臣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Later Zhiyuan he was additionally granted posthumous honors as Honorable Minister Upholding Loyalty, Integrity, and Bright Conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Later Zhiyuan reign he received the additional posthumous title Honorable Minister Upholding Loyalty, Integrity, and Bright Conduct.

sentences.zh: 三子，長曰篤，仕至太中大夫、江東道肅政廉訪副使。

translations.literal: He had three sons; the eldest was named Du, who served up to Grand Master for Grand Harmony and Vice Surveillance Commissioner of the Jiangdong Circuit for Purging Corruption.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons. The eldest, Du, rose to Grand Master for Grand Harmony and Vice Surveillance Commissioner of the Jiangdong Circuit for Purging Corruption.

sentences.zh: ○張炤

translations.literal: ○ Zhang Zhao
translations.idiomatic: ○ Zhang Zhao

sentences.zh: 張炤，字彥明，濟南人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhao, courtesy name Yanming, was a man of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao, whose courtesy name was Yanming, came from Jinan.

sentences.zh: 父信，以商賈起家，貲雄於鄉。

translations.literal: His father Xin rose from merchant trading to establish the family; his wealth dominated the district.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xin had built the family fortune through trade, and his wealth was the greatest in the district.

sentences.zh: 壬辰歲饑，出粟賑貸，鄉人賴以全活。

translations.literal: In the renchen year, when famine struck, he put out grain for relief and loan; fellow villagers relied on this to survive entirely.
translations.idiomatic: In the renchen year, when famine struck, he distributed grain for relief and loan. The people of his district relied on him and survived.

sentences.zh: 炤，幼穎悟力學，始補吏濟南，上計壽陽，行省有積年勾考未輸銀一十萬五千兩，炤條陳利害切至，遂獲免徵，民得無擾。

translations.literal: Zhao, as a child, was bright and studied hard; he first served as a clerk in Jinan; on the annual accounting trip to Shouyang, the Branch Secretariat had long-standing audit arrears of unpaid silver totaling one hundred five thousand taels; Zhao itemized the pros and cons incisively, and then obtained exemption from collection—the people were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was bright and diligent from boyhood. His first appointment was as a clerk in Jinan. On an annual accounting trip to Shouyang, he found that the branch secretariat still owed one hundred five thousand taels in long-standing audit arrears. Zhao laid out the costs and benefits with sharp precision, secured an exemption from collection, and spared the people further hardship.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，辟為中書省掾，俄遷右司提控案牘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong he was recruited as a clerk of the Central Secretariat; soon he was moved to Chief Controller of Records of the Right Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhongtong reign he was recruited as a clerk in the Central Secretariat and was soon promoted to Chief Controller of Records in the Right Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四年，出為山東東路大都督府員外郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was sent out as Outer Section Officer of the Shandong Eastern Circuit Grand General's Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was sent out to serve as Outer Section Officer of the Shandong Eastern Circuit Grand General's Bureau.

sentences.zh: 至元四年，轉陝西五路西蜀四川行中書省左右司員外郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan he was transferred to Outer Section Officer of the Left and Right Secretariats of the Shaanxi Five Circuits and Western Sichuan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Zhiyuan reign he was transferred to Outer Section Officer of the Left and Right Secretariats of the Shaanxi Five Circuits and Western Sichuan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 八年，進階奉訓大夫、知兗州事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to Grand Master for Cherished Instruction and appointed Administrator of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to Grand Master for Cherished Instruction and appointed Administrator of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時州境亢旱，吏民懇禱不雨，炤始至，甘雨沾足。

translations.literal: At the time the prefecture had severe drought; officials and people prayed earnestly without rain; as soon as Zhao arrived, sweet rain soaked abundantly.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture was gripped by severe drought. Officials and commoners prayed without result until Zhao arrived; then a soaking rain fell.

sentences.zh: 聞屬邑有桀黠吏，挾官府肆為暴橫，炤繩之以法，杖出境外，民害遂息。

translations.literal: Hearing that a subordinate county had a fierce and cunning clerk who relied on the government to act violently and overbearingly, Zhao bound him by law, beat him and expelled him beyond the border, and the people's harm then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that a subordinate county harbored a brutal clerk who used official power to terrorize the people, Zhao punished him by law, flogged him, and expelled him beyond the border. The people's suffering then ended.

sentences.zh: 十一年，改授淮西等路行中書省左右司郎中。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was reassigned as Chief Director of the Left and Right Secretariats of the Huai-Xi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was reassigned as Chief Director of the Left and Right Secretariats of the Huai-Xi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丞相阿塔海領軍進攻瓜洲、鎮江，炤運糧儲，給戰具，凡二年，贊畫之力居多。

translations.literal: Chancellor Atahai led the army to attack Guazhou and Zhenjiang; Zhao transported grain stores and supplied war equipment; for two years his contribution in planning was great.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Atahai led the army against Guazhou and Zhenjiang, Zhao handled grain transport and military supplies. For two years his planning made up the greater part of the effort.

sentences.zh: 十三年，揚州未下，丞相阿術提兵攻之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Yangzhou had not yet fallen; Chancellor Aju led troops to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Yangzhou had not yet fallen, and Chancellor Aju led troops to besiege it.

sentences.zh: 五月，宋將李庭芝棄城遁泰州，炤領兵迫揚州城下，躬往招諭，制置硃煥以城降，庭芝亦就擒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Song General Li Tingzhi abandoned the city and fled to Taizhou; Zhao led troops to the walls of Yangzhou, went in person to summon and instruct, Pacification Commissioner Zhu Huan surrendered the city, and Li Tingzhi was also captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Song general Li Tingzhi abandoned Yangzhou and fled to Taizhou. Zhao brought his troops to the city walls, went in person to summon the defenders, and Pacification Commissioner Zhu Huan surrendered the city. Li Tingzhi was captured as well.

sentences.zh: 炤傳檄未下州郡，皆望風款附。

translations.literal: Zhao's proclamations reached the prefectures and commanderies not yet taken, and all looked to the wind and submitted peacefully.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's proclamations reached prefectures and commanderies still holding out, and one after another they submitted without a fight.

sentences.zh: 從阿術入覲，世祖賜錦衣、鞍勒。

translations.literal: Following Aju to enter audience, Shizu bestowed brocade robes and saddle trappings.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Aju to audience with the emperor, Kublai bestowed brocade robes and saddle trappings on him.

sentences.zh: 十三年，升太中大夫、揚州路總管府達魯花赤，商議行中書省事，佩金虎符。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Grand Master for Grand Harmony, Daruqad of the Yangzhou Circuit Chief Administrator's Office, with authority to discuss Branch Secretariat affairs, wearing a golden tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Grand Master for Grand Harmony and appointed Daruqad of the Yangzhou Circuit Chief Administrator's Office with authority to deliberate Branch Secretariat affairs, bearing a golden tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 時行省在揚州，據南北要津，炤撫綏勞來，上下安之。

translations.literal: At the time the Branch Secretariat was at Yangzhou, occupying the vital junction of north and south; Zhao soothed and comforted the people, and above and below were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat was then stationed at Yangzhou, the vital crossing of north and south. Zhao soothed and encouraged the people, and the region settled.

sentences.zh: 十六年，改鎮江路總管府達魯花赤，謝病歸，購書八萬卷，以萬卷送濟南府學資教育。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was changed to Daruqad of the Zhenjiang Circuit Chief Administrator's Office; he resigned because of illness and returned home; he purchased eighty thousand scrolls of books and sent ten thousand scrolls to the Jinan Prefecture School to support education.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to Daruqad of the Zhenjiang Circuit Chief Administrator's Office. Illness forced him to resign and return home. He bought eighty thousand scrolls of books and donated ten thousand to the Jinan Prefecture School to support education.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，起為東昌路總管，蒞政二年，吏民畏服，以治最稱。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was recalled as Chief Administrator of Dongchang Circuit; he governed for two years; officials and people feared and submitted, and his administration was praised as the finest.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was recalled to serve as Chief Administrator of Dongchang Circuit. After two years in office officials and people alike respected him, and his governance was judged the best in the realm.

sentences.zh: 二十五年卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he died, at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 延祐五年，贈太中大夫、東昌路總管，追封清河郡侯，諡敬惠。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yanyou he was posthumously granted Grand Master for Grand Harmony and Chief Administrator of Dongchang Circuit, posthumously enfeoffed Marquis of Qinghe Commandery, posthumous name Jinghui.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Yanyou reign he was posthumously granted the rank of Grand Master for Grand Harmony and the post of Chief Administrator of Dongchang Circuit. He was enfeoffed posthumously as Marquis of Qinghe Commandery with the posthumous name Jinghui.

sentences.zh: 子用中，沂州山場同提舉。

translations.literal: His son Yongzhong served as Associate Intendant of the Yizhou Mountain Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongzhong served as Associate Intendant of the Yizhou Mountain Works.

sentences.zh: ○袁裕

translations.literal: ○ Yuan Yu
translations.idiomatic: ○ Yuan Yu

sentences.zh: 袁裕，字仲寬，洛陽人。

translations.literal: Yuan Yu, courtesy name Zhongkuan, was a man of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yu, whose courtesy name was Zhongkuan, came from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，從兄避難聊城，因家焉。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he followed an elder cousin to flee hardship to Liaocheng and there made his home.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in childhood, he followed an elder cousin to Liaocheng to escape turmoil and settled there.

sentences.zh: 稍長嗜學。

translations.literal: When he grew somewhat older, he loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older he devoted himself to learning.

sentences.zh: 中統初，由聊城縣丞辟中書右司掾，始建言「給重囚衣糧醫藥，免籍其孥、產，止令出焚瘞錢」，後著為令。

translations.literal: In the early Zhongtong era, recruited from Liaocheng County Assistant to clerk of the Right Secretariat of the Central Secretariat, he first proposed: "Give heavy prisoners clothing, grain, and medicine; exempt registering their wives, children, and property; only require payment of the cremation and burial fee"—later this was incorporated as a statute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhongtong era he was recruited from assistant magistrate of Liaocheng County to clerk of the Right Secretariat of the Central Secretariat. He first proposed that heavy prisoners be given clothing, grain, and medicine, that their wives, children, and property not be registered for confiscation, and that they be charged only a cremation and burial fee. The proposal later became law.

sentences.zh: 順天路民王住兒，因鬥誤殺人，其母年七十，言於朝曰：「妾寡且老，恃此兒以為生，兒死，則妾亦死矣。」

translations.literal: Wang Zhu'er, a resident of Shuntian Circuit, in a fight mistakenly killed a man; his mother, aged seventy, addressed the court, saying: "I am a widow and old; I rely on this son for my living; if the son dies, then I too will die."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhu'er, a resident of Shuntian Circuit, had killed a man by mistake in a brawl. His seventy-year-old mother petitioned the court, saying, "I am a widow and old. I depend on this son for my livelihood. If he dies, I die as well."

sentences.zh: 裕言於執政曰：「囚誤殺人，情非故犯，當矜其母，乞宥之。」

translations.literal: Yu told the administrators: "The prisoner mistakenly killed a man; the circumstance is not intentional offense; one ought to pity his mother; I beg pardon for him."
translations.idiomatic: Yu told the chief administrators, "The prisoner killed by mistake, not by design. Pity his mother and grant him pardon."

sentences.zh: 執政以聞，帝從之，囚得免死。

translations.literal: The administrators reported upward; the emperor followed this; the prisoner obtained exemption from death.
translations.idiomatic: The administrators reported to the throne, the emperor agreed, and the prisoner was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 南京總管劉克興掠良民為奴隸，後以矯制獲罪，當籍孥、產之半，裕言於中書，止籍其家，奴隸得復為民者數百。

translations.literal: Liu Kexing, Chief Administrator of Nanjing, plundered good people as slaves; later because of forging an edict he was punished and ought to have half his wives, children, and property registered for confiscation; Yu spoke to the Central Secretariat, and only his household was registered; slaves restored to common people numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kexing, chief administrator of Nanjing, had seized good people as slaves. Later he was punished for forging an edict, and half his family and property should have been confiscated. Yu appealed to the Central Secretariat, which registered only his household. Several hundred enslaved people were restored to common status.

sentences.zh: 至元六年，遷開封府判官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan he was moved to Vice Magistrate of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Zhiyuan reign he was transferred to Vice Magistrate of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 洧川縣達魯花赤貪暴，盛夏役民捕蝗，禁不得飲水，民不勝忿，擊之而斃，有司當以大逆置極刑者七人，連坐者五十餘人。

translations.literal: The Daruqad of Weichuan County was greedy and brutal; in midsummer he conscripted the people to catch locusts and forbade them to drink water; the people could not bear their anger, struck him, and killed him; the authorities wanted to impose capital punishment for great treason on seven men, with more than fifty implicated.
translations.idiomatic: The Daruqad of Weichuan County was greedy and cruel. In midsummer he conscripted the people to catch locusts and forbade them to drink water. Unable to endure it, the people attacked and killed him. The authorities proposed capital punishment for great treason against seven men, with more than fifty others implicated.

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「達魯花赤自犯眾怒而死，安可悉歸罪於民！」

translations.literal: Yu said: "The Daruqad by his own offense aroused public anger and died—how can all guilt be placed on the people!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "The Daruqad brought public wrath on himself and died by his own fault. How can the whole blame fall on the people!"

sentences.zh: 議誅首惡者一人，餘各杖之有差。

translations.literal: It was agreed to execute one chief evildoer; the rest were each beaten with rods according to difference.
translations.idiomatic: Only one ringleader was sentenced to death; the rest received floggings of varying severity.

sentences.zh: 部使者錄囚至縣，疑其太寬，裕辨之益力，遂陳其事狀於中書，刑曹竟從裕議。

translations.literal: A department envoy recording prisoners came to the county and doubted that the sentence was too lenient; Yu argued more forcefully, then reported the facts of the case to the Central Secretariat, and the Penal Bureau finally followed Yu's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: When a departmental envoy reviewing prisoners arrived at the county, he thought the punishment too mild. Yu argued all the more forcefully and reported the case to the Central Secretariat. The Penal Bureau finally upheld Yu's judgment.

sentences.zh: 八年，拜監察御史，俄有旨授西夏中興等路新民安撫副使，兼本道巡行勸農副使、奉直大夫，佩金符。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed censor; soon an edict appointed him Vice Pacification Commissioner of Xingzhong and other circuits of Western Xia for New Residents, concurrently Vice Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture of this circuit, Grand Master for Direct Uprightness, wearing a golden tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed censor. Soon afterward an edict made him Vice Pacification Commissioner of Xingzhong and other circuits of Western Xia for New Residents, concurrently Vice Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture on the same circuit, with the rank of Grand Master for Direct Uprightness and a golden tally.

sentences.zh: 時徙鄂民萬餘於西夏，有司雖與廩食，而流離顛沛猶多。

translations.literal: At the time more than ten thousand people relocated from Ezhou to Western Xia; although the authorities gave grain from storehouses, many still wandered in destitution.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand people had been relocated from Ezhou to Western Xia. Though the authorities issued grain from the storehouses, many still wandered in misery.

sentences.zh: 裕與安撫使獨吉請於朝，計丁給地，立三屯，使耕以自養，官民便之。

translations.literal: Yu together with Pacification Commissioner Duji petitioned the court to count households and grant land, establish three colonies, and make them farm to support themselves; government and people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and Pacification Commissioner Duji petitioned the court to allocate land by household, establish three agricultural colonies, and let the settlers farm for their own support. Both the government and the people benefited.

sentences.zh: 又言：「西夏羌、渾雜居，驅良莫辨，宜驗已有從良書者，則為良民。」

translations.literal: He also said: "In Western Xia Qiang and Hun live mixed together; good people cannot be distinguished when driven away; one ought to verify those who already have certificates of release to common status—then they are good people."
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed, "In Western Xia Qiang and Hun live side by side, and it is hard to tell who has been wrongly seized. Those who already hold certificates of manumission should be recognized as free commoners."

sentences.zh: 從之，得八千餘人，官給牛具，使力田為農。

translations.literal: The court followed this; more than eight thousand people were obtained; the government gave oxen and tools and made them labor the fields as farmers.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved. More than eight thousand people were identified, given oxen and tools by the government, and settled as farmers.

sentences.zh: 十三年，進甘州等路宣撫副使，兼西夏中興等路新民安撫副使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Vice Pacification Commissioner of Ganzhou and other circuits, concurrently Vice Pacification Commissioner of Xingzhong and other circuits of Western Xia for New Residents.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Vice Pacification Commissioner of Ganzhou and other circuits, while retaining his concurrent post as Vice Pacification Commissioner of Xingzhong and other circuits of Western Xia for New Residents.

sentences.zh: 明年，移鎮甘州。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to administer Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to administer Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 十八年，調南陽知府。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to Administrator of Nanyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to Administrator of Nanyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，召拜刑部侍郎，出為順德路總管。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Punishments, then sent out as Chief Administrator of Shunde Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned to serve as Vice Minister of Punishments, then sent out as Chief Administrator of Shunde Circuit.

sentences.zh: 郡有鐵冶提舉張鑑，無子，買妾，其妻妒而殺之。

translations.literal: The circuit had Iron Smelting Intendant Zhang Jian, who had no son; he bought a concubine, and his wife killed her out of jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: In the circuit Iron Smelting Intendant Zhang Jian, who had no son, bought a concubine. His wife killed her in a fit of jealousy.

sentences.zh: 裕捕其妻，訊之服辜。

translations.literal: Yu arrested his wife, questioned her, and she confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Yu arrested the wife, interrogated her, and she confessed to the crime.

sentences.zh: 裕用法平允，而疾惡不少貸如此。

translations.literal: Yu applied the law evenly and fairly, yet hated evil and did not spare offenders in cases like this.
translations.idiomatic: Yu enforced the law with evenhanded fairness, yet in punishing wickedness he rarely showed mercy, as he did here.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，卒於官，年五十九。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he died in office, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he died in office, at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 裕以其兄有鞠育之恩，令其子師愈推廕兄子仁，師癒後仕至侍御史。

translations.literal: Yu, because his elder brother had the grace of raising and nurturing him, had his son Shi Yu recommend hereditary privilege for his brother's son Ren; Shi Yi later served and rose to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Because his elder brother had raised him, Yu had his son Shi Yu secure hereditary privilege for his brother's son Ren. Shi Yi later entered service and rose to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: ○張昉

translations.literal: ○ Zhang Fang
translations.idiomatic: ○ Zhang Fang

sentences.zh: 張昉，字顯卿，東平汶上人。

translations.literal: Zhang Fang, courtesy name Xianqing, was a man of Wen County, Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang, whose courtesy name was Xianqing, came from Wen County in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 父汝明，金大安元年經義進士，官至治書侍御史。

translations.literal: His father Ru Ming passed the jingyi jinshi examination in the first year of the Jin D'ing'an era and rose to Investigation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ru Ming passed the jingyi jinshi examination in the first year of the Jin D'ing'an era and eventually reached the post of Investigation Censor.

sentences.zh: 昉性縝密，遇事敢言，確然有守，以任子試補吏部令史。

translations.literal: Fang was meticulous in disposition, spoke boldly when matters arose, and was resolute in principle; through the son-of-official quota he entered as a trial appointee to clerk of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was meticulous by nature, spoke out boldly when matters arose, and held firmly to his principles. Through the son-of-official quota he entered service as a trial appointee to clerk of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 金亡，還鄉里。

translations.literal: When the Jin fell, he returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Jin, he returned home.

sentences.zh: 嚴實行台東平，辟為掾。

translations.literal: Yan Shi established the Eastern Pacification Commandery as a mobile bureau and recruited him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Shi established the Eastern Pacification Commandery as a mobile bureau, he recruited Fang as an aide.

sentences.zh: 鄉人有執左道惑眾謀不軌者，事覺逮捕，詿誤甚眾，諸僚佐莫敢言，昉獨別白出數百人，實才之，進幕職。

translations.literal: A fellow townsman practiced heterodox doctrine to mislead the masses and plotted rebellion; when the affair was discovered and arrests were made, very many were implicated through error; none of the staff dared speak, but Fang alone distinguished and cleared several hundred people; Shi recognized his talent and promoted him to secretariat staff.
translations.idiomatic: A fellow townsman practiced heterodox teachings to mislead the people and plotted rebellion. When the plot was uncovered and arrests followed, many innocent people were implicated. None of the staff dared speak up, but Fang alone distinguished the guilty from the innocent and cleared several hundred people. Shi recognized his talent and promoted him to secretariat staff.

sentences.zh: 時兵後，吏曹雜進，不習文法，東平轄郡邑五十四，民眾事繁，簿書填委，漫無統紀。

translations.literal: At the time, after the warfare, officials were hastily appointed without knowledge of legal procedure; Dongping governed fifty-four counties and districts, the people were numerous and affairs heavy, documents piled up, and there was no system at all.
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of war, officials had been appointed in haste and knew little of legal procedure. Dongping governed fifty-four counties and districts. The population was large, business was heavy, documents piled up, and there was no order to anything.

sentences.zh: 昉坐曹，躬閱案牘，左酬右答，咸得其當，事無留滯。

translations.literal: Fang sat at his desk, personally reviewing case documents, answering to left and right; all were handled appropriately, and no business was delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Fang sat at his desk and personally reviewed the case files, fielding requests from every side. Everything was handled appropriately, and no business was left pending.

sentences.zh: 初，有將校死事，以弟襲其職者，至是革去，昉辨明，復之，持金夜饋昉，昉卻之，慚謝而去。

translations.literal: Earlier, when military officers died in service, younger brothers had inherited their posts; this practice had now been abolished. Fang clarified the matter and restored it. Someone brought gold by night to present to Fang; Fang refused it, and the man left ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when military officers died in service, their younger brothers had inherited their posts, but that practice had now been abolished. Fang clarified the matter and restored it. One man brought gold by night as a gift; Fang refused it, and the man withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 同里張氏，以絲五萬兩寄昉家而他適，俄而昉家被火，家人惶駭走避，貲用悉焚，惟力完所寄絲，付張氏。

translations.literal: A man surnamed Zhang of the same village deposited fifty thousand liang of silk at Fang's home and went elsewhere; soon Fang's house caught fire, the family fled in panic, and all property was burned, yet they strenuously preserved the deposited silk and returned it to the Zhang family.
translations.idiomatic: A man surnamed Zhang of the same village left fifty thousand liang of silk in Fang's care and went away on business. Soon afterward Fang's house caught fire. The family fled in panic and all their property was burned, yet they managed to preserve the deposited silk intact and returned it to the Zhang family.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，權知東平府事，以疾辭，家居養母。

translations.literal: In a yimao year he served as acting prefect of Dongping; he resigned because of illness and lived at home caring for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In a yimao year he served as acting prefect of Dongping. He then resigned on grounds of illness and remained at home to care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 中統四年，參知中書省事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongtong he became Assistant Manager of Secretariat Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhongtong he was appointed Assistant Manager of Secretariat Affairs.

sentences.zh: 商挺鎮巴蜀，表為四川等處行樞密院參議。

translations.literal: Shang Ting was stationed in Bashu and recommended him as Consultant of the Sichuan Regional Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Shang Ting was stationed in Bashu, he recommended Fang as Consultant of the Sichuan Regional Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，入為中書省左右司郎中，甄別能否，公其黜陟，人無怨言。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan he entered service as Director of the Left and Right Secretariats of the Central Secretariat, assessed ability and incompetence, made promotions and demotions impartially, and no one complained.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiyuan he entered the capital as Director of the Left and Right Secretariats of the Central Secretariat. He assessed who was capable and who was not, made promotions and demotions impartially, and no one raised complaint.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷制國用使司郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Director of the State Revenue Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to Director of the State Revenue Office.

sentences.zh: 制司專職財賦，時宰領之，倚任集事，尤號煩重，昉竭誠贊畫，出納惟謹，賦不加斂，而國用以饒。

translations.literal: The Revenue Office specialized in finances; the chief minister supervised it and relied on it to gather affairs; it was especially called burdensome and heavy. Fang devoted himself wholeheartedly to planning; receipts and disbursements were scrupulously careful; taxes were not increased, yet state revenue became ample.
translations.idiomatic: The Revenue Office handled finances alone, and the chief minister who supervised it relied on it for the most demanding work in government. Fang devoted himself wholeheartedly to planning. Receipts and disbursements were handled with scrupulous care, taxes were not increased, and yet state revenue grew ample.

sentences.zh: 四年，丁內憂，哀毀踰制。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he entered mourning for his mother; his grief and emaciation exceeded the prescribed limits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he entered mourning for his mother, and his grief and self-mortification exceeded what custom prescribed.

sentences.zh: 尋詔起復，錄囚東平，多所平反。

translations.literal: Soon an edict recalled him from mourning; he reviewed prisoners in Dongping and reversed many wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict recalled him from mourning. He reviewed prisoners in Dongping and reversed many wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 七年，轉尚書省左右司郎中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Director of the Left and Right Secretariats of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to Director of the Left and Right Secretariats of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 九年，改中書省左右司郎中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was changed to Director of the Left and Right Secretariats of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was reassigned as Director of the Left and Right Secretariats of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 昉有識慮，損益古今，裁定典憲，時皆宜之，名為稱職。

translations.literal: Fang had foresight and judgment; he added to and subtracted from ancient and modern practice, settled institutions and laws, and all were timely and fitting; he was known as competent in office.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had foresight and sound judgment. He weighed ancient and modern practice, settled institutions and laws, and made decisions suited to the times. He was regarded as fully competent in office.

sentences.zh: 十一年，拜兵刑部尚書，上疏乞骸骨，致其事，卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed Minister of War and Punishments, submitted a memorial requesting retirement, ended his duties, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was appointed Minister of War and Punishments. He submitted a memorial requesting retirement, relinquished his duties, and died.

sentences.zh: 贈中奉大夫、參知政事，追封東平郡公，諡莊憲。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Zhongfeng Grand Master and Assistant Manager of Secretariat Affairs; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Dongping Commandery; canonized Zhuangxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Zhongfeng Grand Master and the post of Assistant Manager of Secretariat Affairs, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Dongping Commandery, and given the posthumous name Zhuangxian.

sentences.zh: 子克遹，平陰縣尹。

translations.literal: His son Ke Yu was magistrate of Pingyin County.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ke Yu served as magistrate of Pingyin County.

sentences.zh: 孫振，秘書著作郎；

translations.literal: His grandson Zhen was Compilation Officer of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zhen served as Compilation Officer of the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 揆，中書省左司都事；

translations.literal: Kui was Commissioner of the Left Secretariat of the Central Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Kui served as Commissioner of the Left Secretariat of the Central Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 拱，常德路蒙古學教授。

translations.literal: Gong was Professor of the Mongolian School of Changde Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: and Gong served as Professor of the Mongolian School of Changde Circuit.

sentences.zh: ○郝彬

translations.literal: ○ Hao Bin
translations.idiomatic: ○ Hao Bin

sentences.zh: 郝彬，字景文，霸州信安人也。

translations.literal: Hao Bin, courtesy name Jingwen, was a man of Xin'an, Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Bin, whose courtesy name was Jingwen, came from Xin'an in Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，年十六，充太子宿衛，擢揚州路治中。

translations.literal: Early in the reign of Shizu, at age sixteen, he served in the Crown Prince's guard corps and was promoted to Vice Prefect of Yangzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Shizu, at the age of sixteen, he entered the Crown Prince's guard corps and was promoted to Vice Prefect of Yangzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 宋末，鄞縣顧閏，聚眾海島，時出攻剽，宋羈縻以官，內附後益橫，侵揚州境，彬討禽之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Song, Gu Run of Yin County gathered followers on sea islands and periodically raided; the Song kept him pacified with office; after submission he grew more arrogant, invaded Yangzhou territory, and Bin captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Song, Gu Run of Yin County gathered followers on offshore islands and periodically launched raids. The Song kept him pacified by granting him office, but after he submitted to the Yuan he grew bolder still and invaded Yangzhou territory. Bin captured him.

sentences.zh: 泰興人有被殺二年而捕賊不獲者，吏誣平人，獄已具。

translations.literal: In Taixing a man had been murdered for two years without the thief being caught; officials framed an innocent man, and the case was settled.
translations.idiomatic: In Taixing a man had been murdered two years earlier and the killer still had not been caught. Officials framed an innocent man, and the case was already settled.

sentences.zh: 彬疑其誣，讞之，果得真賊。

translations.literal: Bin suspected a false accusation, referred the case upward, and indeed found the real thief.
translations.idiomatic: Bin suspected a false accusation, referred the case upward for review, and the real culprit was found.

sentences.zh: 御史薦彬同知淮西道宣慰司事，核戶版，理屯田，諸廢修舉。

translations.literal: A censor recommended Bin as Vice Commissioner of the Huaidao Pacification Commission; he verified household registers, managed military colonies, and restored abandoned projects.
translations.idiomatic: A censor recommended Bin for the post of Vice Commissioner of the Huaidao Pacification Commission. He verified household registers, managed military colonies, and restored projects that had fallen into neglect.

sentences.zh: 江淮財賦總管府掌東宮田賦，其官屬皆從詹事院奏授，不隸中書，往往為奸利，誅求無厭。

translations.literal: The Jianghuai Revenue General Office managed the Crown Prince's field taxes; its officials were all appointed on memorial from the Crown Prince Household Office and did not belong to the Central Secretariat; they often profited corruptly and extorted without limit.
translations.idiomatic: The Jianghuai Revenue General Office managed the Crown Prince's field taxes. Its officials were appointed on memorial from the Crown Prince Household Office rather than through the Central Secretariat, and they often used their posts for private profit, extorting the people without end.

sentences.zh: 彬為總管，入見，請受憲司糾察以革私弊，罷所隸六提舉司以蘇民瘼。

translations.literal: When Bin became General Manager, on audience he requested to be subject to Surveillance Commission inspection to reform private abuses, and to abolish the six sub-offices under its jurisdiction to relieve the people's suffering.
translations.idiomatic: When Bin became General Manager, he appeared at court and asked that his office be subject to Surveillance Commission inspection in order to root out private abuses. He also requested the abolition of the six sub-offices under its jurisdiction to relieve the people's suffering.

sentences.zh: 從之，遂罷​​其四。

translations.literal: The court agreed, and four of them were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the request, and four of the six sub-offices were abolished.

sentences.zh: 國家經費，鹽利居十之八，而兩淮鹽獨當天下之半，法日以壞，以彬行戶部尚書經理之。

translations.literal: Of state revenue, salt profits accounted for eight parts in ten, and Liang-Huai salt alone bore half the empire; the law daily deteriorated, and Bin was appointed acting Minister of Revenue to manage it.
translations.idiomatic: Salt profits accounted for eight tenths of state revenue, and Liang-Huai salt alone supplied half the empire. As the system grew daily more corrupt, Bin was appointed acting Minister of Revenue to reform it.

sentences.zh: 彬請度舟楫所通、道里所均，建六倉，煮鹽於場，運積之倉；

translations.literal: Bin requested assessing where boats could pass and where distances were even, building six warehouses, boiling salt at the fields, and transporting it to accumulate in warehouses;
translations.idiomatic: Bin proposed surveying where waterways were navigable and routes were evenly spaced, building six warehouses, boiling salt at the production sites, and transporting it for storage;

sentences.zh: 歲首，聽群商於轉運司探倉籌定其所，乃買券，又定河商、江商市易之不如法者，著為法。

translations.literal: at the year's start, allowing merchants to inspect the warehouses at the Transport Office and fix their locations, then buy certificates; he also regulated river merchants and river-boat merchants who traded improperly, and established this as law.
translations.idiomatic: permitting merchants at the year's start to inspect the warehouses at the Transport Office and choose their locations before purchasing certificates. He also regulated improper trading by river merchants and river-boat merchants and incorporated the rules into law.

sentences.zh: 入為工部尚書，改戶部尚書，拜中書參知政事，俄免歸。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Minister of Works, was changed to Minister of Revenue, was appointed Assistant Manager of the Central Secretariat, and soon was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Minister of Works, was transferred to Minister of Revenue, and was appointed Assistant Manager of the Central Secretariat, but soon was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 尚書省立，拜參知政事，辭不獲命。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Revenue was established, he was appointed Assistant Manager of Secretariat Affairs; he declined but could not refuse the order.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Revenue was established, he was again appointed Assistant Manager of Secretariat Affairs. He declined, but the order could not be refused.

sentences.zh: 同列務生事要功，殺無罪之人，彬積誠意開引，或從或違，橫不可製。

translations.literal: His colleagues sought to manufacture affairs to win merit and killed innocent people; Bin sincerely and repeatedly remonstrated with them; some listened and some did not; their excesses could not be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues manufactured affairs to win credit and killed innocent people. Bin remonstrated with them sincerely and at length. Some listened and some did not, and their excesses could not be checked.

sentences.zh: 命兼大司徒，不拜。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve concurrently as Grand Minister of Agriculture; he did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to serve concurrently as Grand Minister of Agriculture, but he refused to accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 仁宗在東宮，彬懇辭至力，因稱疾篤。

translations.literal: When Renzong was at the Eastern Palace, Bin declined with utmost earnestness and therefore claimed grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: While Renzong was still at the Eastern Palace, Bin declined the appointment with all the force he could muster and then claimed grave illness.

sentences.zh: 時相強起之，至奏重賜以餌之，彬不為動。

translations.literal: The chief minister forcibly tried to recall him, even memorializing heavy rewards to entice him, but Bin was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister forcibly tried to recall him and even memorialized for lavish rewards to entice him, but Bin would not be moved.

sentences.zh: 議罪之，罪無從得，彬堅臥一榻至數月，尚書省臣皆得罪，彬不與焉。

translations.literal: They debated punishing him, but no crime could be found; Bin lay rigidly on one couch for several months; the officials of the Ministry of Revenue were all punished, but Bin was not among them.
translations.idiomatic: They debated punishing him, but no charge could be made to stick. Bin lay on a single couch for months on end. When the officials of the Ministry of Revenue were all punished, Bin was not among them.

sentences.zh: 家居七年，足跡未嘗一出門外。

translations.literal: He lived at home for seven years, and his footsteps never once went outside the door.
translations.idiomatic: He remained at home for seven years and never once set foot outside his door.

sentences.zh: 仁宗思之，以為大司農卿，未幾，謝病。

translations.literal: Renzong missed him and appointed him Grand Minister of Agriculture; before long he resigned citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong missed him and appointed him Grand Minister of Agriculture, but before long Bin resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 延祐七年三月卒。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year of Yanyou he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third month of the seventh year of Yanyou.

sentences.zh: ○高源

translations.literal: ○ Gao Yuan
translations.idiomatic: ○ Gao Yuan

sentences.zh: 高源，字仲淵，晉州人。

translations.literal: Gao Yuan, courtesy name Zhongyuan, was a man of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yuan, whose courtesy name was Zhongyuan, came from Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖揖，為州法吏，用法公平。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yi was a district legal clerk and applied the law fairly.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yi served as a district legal clerk and applied the law with fairness.

sentences.zh: 父汝霖，為真定廉訪司照磨，使東平，道高唐，遇盜死。

translations.literal: His father Ru Lin was recording secretary of the Zhending Investigation Commission; traveling on mission to Dongping, on the road at Gaotang he met bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ru Lin served as recording secretary of the Zhending Investigation Commission. While traveling on mission to Dongping, he was killed by bandits at Gaotang.

sentences.zh: 源幼力學，事母孝，補縣吏。

translations.literal: Yuan studied hard from youth, was filial in serving his mother, and entered service as a county clerk.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yuan applied himself to learning, served his mother with filial devotion, and entered service as a county clerk.

sentences.zh: 中統初，擢衛輝路知事，累升齊河縣尹，有遺愛，去官十年，民猶立碑頌之。

translations.literal: Early in Zhongtong he was promoted to assistant of Weihui Circuit, rose in succession to magistrate of Qihe County, left a legacy of affection, and ten years after leaving office the people still erected a stele praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhongtong era he was promoted to assistant of Weihui Circuit and eventually rose to magistrate of Qihe County. The people cherished him, and ten years after he left office they still erected a stele in his praise.

sentences.zh: 遷行台都事，僉江南浙西道提刑按察司事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief of Staff of the Mobile Bureau and appointed to the Jiangnan Zhexi Circuit Investigation and Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chief of Staff of the Mobile Bureau and appointed to the Jiangnan Zhexi Circuit Investigation and Surveillance Commission.

sentences.zh: 劾常州路達魯花赤馬恕奪民田及他不法事。

translations.literal: He impeached Ma Nu, darughachi of Changzhou Circuit, for seizing commoners' land and other unlawful acts.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Ma Nu, the darughachi of Changzhou Circuit, for seizing commoners' land and other unlawful acts.

sentences.zh: 恕懼，走賂權臣阿合馬，以他事誣源。

translations.literal: Nu feared this, fled to bribe the powerful minister Ahmad, and framed Yuan on other charges.
translations.idiomatic: Nu was afraid and fled to bribe the powerful minister Ahmad, who then framed Yuan on other charges.

sentences.zh: 既係獄，一日，忽釋之，莫知所由。

translations.literal: After he was imprisoned, one day he was suddenly released, and no one knew why.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan was imprisoned, he was suddenly released one day, and no one knew why.

sentences.zh: 先時，源所居鄰里，多阿合馬姻戚，素知源事母至孝。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the neighborhood where Yuan lived, many were Ahmad's relatives by marriage and had long known that Yuan served his mother with utmost filiality.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, many of Ahmad's relatives by marriage had lived in Yuan's neighborhood and had long known how filial he was toward his mother.

sentences.zh: 至是，聞源坐非辜，悉詣阿合馬曰：「源，孝子也，非但我知之，天必知之。

translations.literal: At this time, hearing that Yuan sat in wrongful guilt, they all went to Ahmad and said: "Yuan is a filial son; not only we know it--Heaven must know it.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard that Yuan had been wrongfully imprisoned, they all went to Ahmad and said, "Yuan is a filial son. It is not only we who know this--Heaven knows it as well.

sentences.zh: 況媒孽之罪非實，若妄殺源，悖天不祥。」

translations.literal: Moreover the crime of false accusation is not real; if you rashly kill Yuan, it is contrary to Heaven and inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the charges against him are false. If you kill Yuan without cause, you will defy Heaven and bring misfortune upon yourself."

sentences.zh: 阿合馬感悟，得不死。

translations.literal: Ahmad was moved by this and Yuan was not killed.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by their words, Ahmad spared Yuan's life.

sentences.zh: 尋除河間等路都轉運副使，撫治有條，灶戶逃者皆復業，常賦外，羨餘幾十萬緡。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Deputy Transport Commissioner of Hejian Circuit and others; his governance was orderly; salt-household deserters all returned to their occupations; beyond regular taxes there was a surplus of nearly several hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Deputy Transport Commissioner of Hejian Circuit and other circuits. He governed in an orderly way, salt-household deserters all returned to their work, and beyond the regular taxes he produced a surplus of nearly several hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 至元二十四年，為江東道勸農營田使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Zhiyuan he became Commissioner for Agricultural Encouragement and Colony Management of Jiangdong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Zhiyuan he was appointed Commissioner for Agricultural Encouragement and Colony Management of Jiangdong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，遷都水監。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was transferred to Supervisor of Waterworks.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was transferred to Supervisor of Waterworks.

sentences.zh: 開通惠河，由文明門東七十里，與會通河接，置閘七、橋十二，人蒙其利。

translations.literal: He opened the Tonghui Canal from seventy li east of Civilization Gate, connecting with the Hui Tong River; he set seven locks and twelve bridges, and the people benefited.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the Tonghui Canal from a point seventy li east of Civilization Gate, connecting it with the Hui Tong River. He installed seven locks and twelve bridges, and the people reaped the benefit.

sentences.zh: 授同知湖南道宣慰司事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Hunan Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Hunan Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 子夢弼、良弼、公弼。

translations.literal: His sons were Mengbi, Liangbi, and Gongbi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Mengbi, Liangbi, and Gongbi.

sentences.zh: ○楊湜

translations.literal: ○ Yang Shi
translations.idiomatic: ○ Yang Shi

sentences.zh: 楊湜，字彥清，真定藁城人。

translations.literal: Yang Shi, courtesy name Yanqing, was a man of Gaocheng, Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shi, whose courtesy name was Yanqing, came from Gaocheng in Zhending.

sentences.zh: 習章程學，工書算，始以府吏遷檢法。

translations.literal: He studied regulatory learning, was skilled in writing and calculation, and began as a prefectural clerk before being transferred to legal inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He studied regulatory learning and was skilled in writing and calculation. He began as a prefectural clerk and was later transferred to legal inspector.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，辟為中書掾，與中山楊珍、無極楊卞齊名，時人以三楊目之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong he was recruited as an aide of the Central Secretariat; together with Yang Zhen of Zhongshan and Yang Bian of Wuji he was equally famous, and people of the time called them the Three Yangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong he was recruited as an aide of the Central Secretariat. Together with Yang Zhen of Zhongshan and Yang Bian of Wuji he was equally renowned, and people of the time called them the Three Yangs.

sentences.zh: 中書省初立，國用不足，湜論鈔法宜以榷貨制國用，朝廷從之，因俾掌其條製。

translations.literal: When the Central Secretariat was first established, state revenue was insufficient; Shi argued that the paper-money system ought to use monopoly trade to fund state revenue; the court agreed and therefore had him manage its regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When the Central Secretariat was first established, state revenue was insufficient. Shi argued that the paper-money system should be used to fund the state through monopoly trade. The court agreed and put him in charge of drafting the regulations.

sentences.zh: 四年，授益都路宣慰司諮議，遷左司提控掾，請嚴贓吏法。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Consultant of the Yidu Circuit Pacification Commission, was transferred to Control Aide of the Left Secretariat, and requested strict laws against corrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Consultant of the Yidu Circuit Pacification Commission and was transferred to Control Aide of the Left Secretariat, where he requested strict laws against corrupt officials.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，除河南大名諸處行中書省都事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan he was appointed Chief Staff Officer of the Henan-Daming Regional Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhiyuan he was appointed Chief Staff Officer of the Henan-Daming Regional Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年，立制國用司，總天下錢穀，以湜為員外郎，佩金符。

translations.literal: In the third year the State Revenue Office was established to aggregate the empire's finances; Shi was appointed Vice Director and wore a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the State Revenue Office was established to oversee the empire's finances. Shi was appointed Vice Director and was granted a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 改宣徽院參議。

translations.literal: He was changed to Consultant of the Imperial Household Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Consultant of the Imperial Household Commission.

sentences.zh: 湜計帑立籍，具其出入之算，每月終上之，遂定為令。

translations.literal: Shi inventoried the treasury and established ledgers, setting out calculations of income and expenditure and submitting them at each month's end; this was then fixed as a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Shi inventoried the treasury and established ledgers detailing income and expenditure, submitting accounts at the end of each month. The practice was then fixed as a regulation.

sentences.zh: 加諸路交鈔都提舉，上鈔法便宜事，謂平準行用庫白金出入，有偷濫之弊，請以五十兩鑄為錠，文以元寶，用之便。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Chief Inspector of Paper Money Circuits and submitted conveniences for the paper-money system, saying that the stable-circulation warehouses' white-silver receipts and disbursements had abuses of theft and dilution; he requested casting fifty-liang ingots marked as yuanbao, which would be convenient to use.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed Chief Inspector of Paper Money Circuits and submitted proposals to improve the paper-money system. He said the stable-circulation warehouses suffered theft and dilution in their handling of white silver, and requested that fifty-liang ingots marked as yuanbao be cast for easier use.

sentences.zh: 七年，改制國用司為尚書省，拜戶部侍郎，仍兼交鈔提舉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the State Revenue Office was changed to the Ministry of Revenue; he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and still concurrently served as Chief Inspector of Paper Money.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the State Revenue Office was reorganized as the Ministry of Revenue. He was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue while retaining his concurrent post as Chief Inspector of Paper Money.

sentences.zh: 時用壬子舊籍定民賦役之高下，湜言：「貧富不常，歲久浸易，其可以昔時之籍，而定今之賦役哉！」

translations.literal: At the time the renzi old register was used to fix the high and low of people's taxes and corvee; Shi said: "Rich and poor are not constant; over years they gradually change--how can one use the register of former times to fix present taxes and corvee!"
translations.idiomatic: At the time the renzi household register was used to fix people's tax and corvee obligations. Shi said, "Wealth and poverty are not fixed. Over the years they gradually shift. How can a register from former times be used to fix present taxes and corvee obligations?"

sentences.zh: 廷議善之，因俾第其輕重，人以為平。

translations.literal: The court discussion praised this, and therefore had him rank their lightness and heaviness; people considered it fair.
translations.idiomatic: The court discussion approved his view and had him rank obligations by degree of burden. People regarded the result as fair.

sentences.zh: 湜心計精析，時論經費者，咸推其能焉。

translations.literal: Shi had a precise and analytical mind for calculation; when people of the time discussed state finances, all praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Shi had a precise and analytical mind for financial calculation, and whenever people of the time discussed state finances they praised his ability.

sentences.zh: 子克忠，安豐路總管。

translations.literal: His son Kezhong was General Manager of Anfeng Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kezhong served as General Manager of Anfeng Circuit.

sentences.zh: 孫貞。

translations.literal: His grandson was Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson was Zhen.

sentences.zh: ○吳鼎

translations.literal: ○ Wu Ding
translations.idiomatic: ○ Wu Ding

sentences.zh: 吳鼎，字鼎臣，燕人。

translations.literal: Wu Ding, courtesy name Dingchen, was a man of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ding, whose courtesy name was Dingchen, came from Yan.

sentences.zh: 至元十七年，見裕宗於東宮，命入宿衛。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Zhiyuan he met Crown Prince Zong at the Eastern Palace and was ordered to enter guard service.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Zhiyuan he was received by Crown Prince Zong at the Eastern Palace and ordered to enter the guard corps.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，授織染雜造局總管府副總管，後積官至禮部尚書、宣徽副使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed Deputy General Manager of the Dyeing and Miscellaneous Manufactures Bureau; later he accumulated offices to Minister of Rites and Vice Commissioner of the Imperial Household Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed Deputy General Manager of the Dyeing and Miscellaneous Manufactures Bureau. He later rose through successive posts to Minister of Rites and Vice Commissioner of the Imperial Household Commission.

sentences.zh: 太德十一年，山東諸郡飢，詔鼎往賑之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dade, the circuits of Shandong suffered famine; an edict ordered Ding to go relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Dade the circuits of Shandong suffered famine, and an edict ordered Ding to go and provide relief.

sentences.zh: 朝廷議發米四萬石，鈔折米一萬石，鼎謂同使者曰：「民得鈔，將何從易米？」

translations.literal: The court planned to issue forty thousand shi of grain and ten thousand shi equivalent in paper money; Ding told the fellow envoy: "If the people receive paper money, how will they obtain grain to exchange for it?"
translations.idiomatic: The court planned to distribute forty thousand shi of grain and paper money equivalent to ten thousand shi of grain. Ding told his fellow envoy, "If the people receive paper money, where will they get grain to exchange for it?"

sentences.zh: 同使者曰：「朝議已定，恐不可復得。」

translations.literal: The fellow envoy said: "The court's decision is settled; I fear it cannot be changed."
translations.idiomatic: His fellow envoy said, "The court's decision is already settled. I fear it cannot be changed."

sentences.zh: 鼎曰：「人命豈不重於米耶！」

translations.literal: Ding said: "Are human lives not heavier than grain!"
translations.idiomatic: Ding replied, "Are human lives not worth more than grain?"

sentences.zh: 言於朝，卒從所請。

translations.literal: He spoke to the court, and in the end his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He appealed to the court, and in the end his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，改正奉大夫、保定路總管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida he was promoted to Zhengfeng Grand Master and General Manager of Baoding Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhida he was promoted to Zhengfeng Grand Master and appointed General Manager of Baoding Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時皇太后欲幸五台，言者請開保定西五回嶺，以取捷徑。

translations.literal: At the time the empress dowager wished to visit Wutai; memorializers requested opening Wuhui Ridge west of Baoding to take a shortcut.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the empress dowager wished to visit Mount Wutai, and memorializers proposed opening Wuhui Ridge west of Baoding as a shortcut.

sentences.zh: 遣使即鼎，使視地形，計工費，鼎言：「荒山斗入，人跡久絕，非乘輿所宜往。」

translations.literal: An envoy was sent to Ding to have him inspect the terrain and estimate labor costs; Ding said: "Barren mountains rise steeply, human tracks have long ceased—this is not a place the imperial carriage ought to go."
translations.idiomatic: An envoy was sent to Ding to survey the terrain and estimate the cost of the work. Ding said, "The mountains are barren and rise steeply, and human traffic has long ceased. It is not a route fit for the imperial carriage."

sentences.zh: 還報，太后喜，為寢其役。

translations.literal: He returned to report; the empress dowager was pleased and suspended the project.
translations.idiomatic: He reported back, and the empress dowager was pleased and abandoned the project.

sentences.zh: 三年，召授資善大夫、同知中政院事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was summoned and appointed Grand Master for Excellent Goodness and Vice Director of the Central Government Affairs Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was summoned and appointed Grand Master for Excellent Goodness and Vice Director of the Central Government Affairs Court.

sentences.zh: 兩浙財賦隸中政者巨萬計，前往者率多取其贏，鼎治之，一無私焉。

translations.literal: The revenues of the Two Zhes under the Central Government Affairs Court amounted to tens of millions; those who went there mostly took their profit—Ding governed it without a trace of private gain.
translations.idiomatic: The Two Zhes' revenues under the Central Government Affairs Court ran to tens of millions, and officials sent there usually skimmed profits for themselves. Ding administered the office without taking anything for himself.

sentences.zh: 浙有兩富豪，曰硃、張家，多貸與民錢，其後兩家誅沒，而券之已償者，亦入於官，官唯驗券徵理，民不能堪。

translations.literal: In Zhe there were two wealthy houses, the Zhu and Zhang families, who had lent much money to the people; afterward both families were executed and their property confiscated, and even bonds already repaid were taken into official hands—the authorities only verified bonds and demanded payment, and the people could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhe two wealthy houses, the Zhu and Zhang families, had lent heavily to the people. Later both families were executed and their property confiscated, and even receipts for debts already repaid were seized by the state. Officials enforced payment by bond alone, and the people could not endure it.

sentences.zh: 鼎力為辨白，始獲免。

translations.literal: Ding strove to clarify the matter on their behalf, and only then were they exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Ding argued strenuously on their behalf, and only then were they released from the demand.

sentences.zh: 四年，改京畿澧運使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was changed to Transport Commissioner of the Capital Region.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Transport Commissioner of the Capital Region.

sentences.zh: 皇慶二年，特旨复僉宣徵院事；

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangqing, by special decree he was again appointed to administer the Bureau of Palace Provisions;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangqing, by special imperial order he was again appointed to administer the Bureau of Palace Provisions;

sentences.zh: 四月，進資政大夫、崇祥院使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he was promoted to Grand Master for Governance Assistance and Director of the Court of August Felicity.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he was promoted to Grand Master for Governance Assistance and Director of the Court of August Felicity.

sentences.zh: 延祐三年卒，年五十有三。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanyou he died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yanyou he died, aged fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈榮祿大夫、平章政事、柱國，追封薊國公，諡孝敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of Glory and Blessing, Grand Administrator of the Secretariat, and Pillar of the State, enfeoffed as Duke of Ji, with the posthumous title Xiaomin.
