translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of Glory and Blessing, Grand Administrator of the Secretariat, and Pillar of the State, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Ji, with the posthumous title Xiaomin.

sentences.zh: ○梁德圭

translations.literal: ○ Liang Degui
translations.idiomatic: ○ Liang Degui

sentences.zh: 梁德圭，字伯溫，大興良鄉人。

translations.literal: Liang Degui, styled Bowen, was a man of Liangxiang in Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Degui, whose courtesy name was Bowen, came from Liangxiang in Daxing.

sentences.zh: 初給事昭睿順聖皇后宮，令習國語，通奏對。

translations.literal: At first he served in the palace of Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng and was ordered to study the national language, becoming skilled at memorial audience.
translations.idiomatic: He began as an attendant in the palace of Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng, was instructed to study Mongolian, and became adept at audience with the throne.

sentences.zh: 年十一，見世祖。

translations.literal: At age eleven he was received by the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he was received in audience by Kublai.

sentences.zh: 至元十六年，為中書左司員外郎，俄升郎中，六遷至參議尚書省事。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan he was Vice Director in the Left Department of the Secretariat, soon promoted to Director, and after six transfers reached Commissioner for Deliberation on Secretariat Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan he served as Vice Director in the Left Department of the Secretariat, was soon promoted to Director, and after six further appointments reached Commissioner for Deliberation on Secretariat Affairs.

sentences.zh: 至元三十一年，執政入奏事，帝詢其曲折，不能對，德圭從旁辯析，明白通暢，帝大悅，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Zhiyuan a chief administrator entered to report affairs; the emperor asked the details and he could not answer; Degui from the side analyzed and explained clearly and fluently; the emperor was greatly pleased and appointed him Vice Administrator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year of Zhiyuan a chief administrator came to report on affairs, but when the emperor asked for details he could not answer. Degui explained from the side with clarity and fluency. The emperor was greatly pleased and appointed him Vice Administrator of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 在省日久，凡錢穀出納之制，銓選進退之宜，諸籓賜予之節，命有驟至，不暇閱簡牘，同列莫知措辭，德圭數語即定；

translations.literal: Having long been in the secretariat, he knew all regulations for revenue disbursement, standards for appointments and dismissals, and protocols for grants to the princely domains; when orders came suddenly and there was no time to consult documents, his colleagues did not know how to phrase replies—Degui settled matters in a few words;
translations.idiomatic: After long service in the secretariat he knew every rule governing revenue, appointments and dismissals, and grants to the princely domains. When sudden orders arrived with no time to consult documents and his colleagues did not know how to respond, Degui settled the matter in a few words;

sentences.zh: 間遇疑事，則曰某事當如某律，某年嘗有此旨，驗之皆然。

translations.literal: when he occasionally met doubtful matters he would say such-and-such a matter ought to follow such-and-such a statute, in such-and-such a year there was once such an edict—and on verification it was always so.
translations.idiomatic: When doubtful cases arose he would say that a given matter should follow a given statute, or that an edict on the subject had been issued in a given year—and verification always proved him right.

sentences.zh: 北京地震，帝閱州郡報囚之數，怪其過多，德圭方在右司，詔問焉。

translations.literal: When Beijing suffered an earthquake, the emperor reviewed the numbers of prisoners reported by prefectures and commanderies and marveled that they were excessive; Degui was then in the Right Department, and an edict questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Beijing was struck by an earthquake, the emperor reviewed prisoner counts reported from the prefectures and found them alarmingly high. Degui was serving in the Right Department at the time, and the emperor questioned him by edict.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「當國者急於徵索，蔓延收系，以致此爾。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Those in charge of the state are urgent in collection and seizure, and arrests spread widely—this has led to it."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Those governing the state are overzealous in collection and seizure, and arrests have spread everywhere until this is the result."

sentences.zh: 帝感悟，為大赦中外逋負，民賴以蘇。

translations.literal: The emperor was enlightened, proclaimed a great amnesty for arrears within and without, and the people relied on this to recover.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the point to heart, proclaimed a great amnesty for debts and arrears throughout the realm, and the people were able to recover.

sentences.zh: 大德間，成宗即位，一遵祖武，廟堂以安靜為治，求進者不得逞其志，朋聚興怨，摭事中傷德圭。

translations.literal: During Dade, when Chengzong ascended, he wholly followed his ancestor's martial way; the court took quiet as its governance, and those seeking advancement could not realize their aims—they banded together in resentment and seized on affairs to slander Degui.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dade reign Chengzong succeeded to the throne and followed his grandfather's policies in full. The court governed by quietism, and those eager for advancement could not achieve their aims. They banded together in resentment and seized on incidents to slander Degui.

sentences.zh: 會帝有疾，言者盛氣致詰，德圭以位居執政，不受凌轢，慷慨引咎，遂安置湖廣。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell ill, the accusers came with fierce air to interrogate; Degui, holding the rank of chief administrator, would not accept bullying, boldly took blame upon himself, and was then posted to Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, his accusers confronted him with fierce aggression. Degui, holding high office, refused to be bullied, boldly accepted blame, and was posted to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 帝疾愈，問知之，召使復位。

translations.literal: When the emperor's illness recovered, he asked and learned of it, and summoned him to resume his post.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor recovered and learned what had happened, he summoned Degui back to his post.

sentences.zh: 既至，帝問：「卿安在？」

translations.literal: When he arrived, the emperor asked: "Where have you been?"
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, the emperor asked, "Where have you been?"

sentences.zh: 德圭涕泣不能語。

translations.literal: Degui wept and could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Degui wept and could not speak.

sentences.zh: 賜酒饌，使往拜其母，因以氣疾，乞骸骨歸。

translations.literal: He was granted wine and food and sent to pay respects to his mother; because of a breathing ailment he begged to return home with his bones.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him wine and food and sent him to visit his mother. Citing a respiratory ailment, he then begged to retire and return home.

sentences.zh: 大德八年九月，卒於家，年四十有六。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighth year of Dade he died at home, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eighth year of Dade he died at home, aged forty-six.
